- **UI overhaul, slice 3, part two: a part dropped on a weapon fits it, 2026-10-24 (C3 of the
  three-features plan, `/mnt/project-files/planning/2026-10-24_three-features.md`).**
  `SimGunsmith.drop_slot` answers with the first empty slot a held part `fits`, for a survivor who
  may work on that part here, or "" for none. The inventory sheet asks it on release and on hover:
  over a weapon in the grid or in an equipment box, a fit is the accent wash (`Locker.fit`) and
  the release pushes `item.attach`; anywhere else the drop is the ordinary grid placement. An
  occupied slot is never swapped by a drop. Gate: `godot:check:inventory` FIT-DROP (an empty
  magazine slot takes the spare, on the grid plate or a worn rifle's box, and the hover says so; a bipod the hands cannot fit goes to the
  grid over a free underbarrel; a second magazine on a full rifle goes to the grid). Sabotage
  checked: removing the hands-or-bench test turns the bipod lane red. The hover is shown by the
  review scene `bench_drop` (`godot:check:shots` lists it; `planning/ui-slice-3/c3_drop_fit_*.png`
  at both sizes, no before shot since the drop-to-fit did not exist on main). The call is in
  docs/30, "A dropped part fits only an empty slot".

- **UI overhaul, slice 3: menus and the E prompt speak one grammar, 2026-10-24 (C4 of the
  three-features plan, `/mnt/project-files/planning/2026-10-24_three-features.md`).** **The
  finding:** the plan assumed the action bar's E clause and the menu's in-reach row both came from
  `SimFortify.rung_of`. They did not. `ui/hud.gd`'s `_reach_clause` led with the look-at, so facing
  a boarded window the bar said "E — intact" (the board's state) while E boarded it and the menu
  said "board up the window"; at a door the bar said nothing while E opened it and the menu said
  "open the door"; and main.gd's context line was the fallback, so a state could stand under E
  wherever nothing else spoke. **The fix:** `SimContext.reach_words`, appended to
  `godot/sim/context.gd`, walks `_use_context`'s ladder in its own order (the loose item, the
  container, the door, the stranger, the car, then `rung_of`) in the words `verbs_at` writes for the
  same row, and `_reach_clause` asks it (from a seat, the car's own clause). `action_line` lost its
  `look` and `hint` arguments; the states still reach the survivor's lines through `hint`.
  **The header:** `SimContext.target_label` ("Mara Sato", "you", "the crate", "the tin's name", "the
  door", "a zombie" whatever kind it is, nothing for the ground) is drawn above the rows in the
  small dim ink with a groove under it, by `ItemMenu`'s own `size_of`, `draw_menu` and `verb_rects`
  taking an optional header, so the loot sheet's menu keeps its shape and both menus still wear one
  steel. **The keys:** with the menu open, `input_map.gd` hands keys to `context_menu.gd`'s `key()`
  first; an amber ring opens on the first row, Up and Down move it and wrap, Enter dispatches the
  ringed row through `main._context_pick`, Escape closes with nothing sent, any other key closes it
  and does what it does, and the ring follows the pointer. The ringed row is the street menu's one
  amber row (`ItemMenu.row_colour`; the loot sheet's menu keeps its lead verbs lit), and the menu
  opens on the art grid and stops above the HUD's action bar however low the click. **Gates:** `godot:check:context` gains
  HEADER (each label, a colonist by the whole name, the ground's absence, rows under the header, a
  headerless menu unchanged, the ink following the ring),
  BAR (the bar's E clause equals the menu's first row at a boarded window, a shut and an open door,
  a loose tin and a crate; the board's state is not that row) and KEYS on the scene's own menu (the ring
  opens on row one, Down, Up and both wraps, Down then Enter pushes row two's command and closes,
  an arrow walks nobody, Escape sends nothing, a click on the header picks nothing, the ground's
  menu has no header); RIGHT-CLICK clicks a row by the menu's own `row_rects`.
  `godot:check:play` gains MENU-ESCAPE: a menu opened low at 1280×720 ends above the action bar and
  on the grid, a right click on yourself opens a menu headed "you",
  Escape closes it and raises no screen, and with no menu the same key still pauses.
  `godot:check:hud`'s ACTION lane runs on a real map: E names "board up the window" at a boarded
  window and never the board's state; RUNG follows `_reach_clause` to `reach_words` and
  `reach_words` to `rung_of`. A review scene, `context_menu` (a crate right-clicked on the street,
  its verify holding the header, the first row and the bar's E clause together), joins
  `godot/review/scenes.gd`. Sabotage checked: the door taken out of `reach_words` (BAR), the bar
  back on the look-at (BAR), the header not passed (HEADER), Down and Up made no-ops (KEYS), Enter
  dispatching nothing (KEYS), and Escape no longer spent on the menu (MENU-ESCAPE) each turn their
  lane red. **Not done:** `verbs_at`'s door row is offered for a broken door, and for an open one
  somebody stands in, where E does nothing (`_door_would_toggle` refuses); the plan kept this slice
  out of `verbs_at`, so the fix is a follow-up. No UI draw cost was measured. The shots of the
  merged head (fe6d3a60), `context_menu` at both windows, are in the project's
  `planning/ui-slice-3/c4/`; they match the shots the art review judged byte for byte.

- **Kernel & tooling — the playbook and the init audit, 2026-10-23.** The owner asked for the
  repository to be initialised for agents and for one playbook every agent can read. An audit of
  the build, test and gate commands against `CLAUDE.md` added three things to it: the commands for
  one gate, one CI shard and one oracle test file; a short "How the code fits together" section
  (the 20 Hz ECS and its phases, modules registering through `SimBoot.register_playable_modules`,
  presentation reading only through read models, and the five places a new gate touches); and
  `scripts/m2-shards.mjs` with `check:shards` in the routing table's gate row. docs/38 is the
  playbook (how the project runs, linked from the top of `CLAUDE.md`), and `AGENTS.md` came back
  as a pointer with no content of its own (docs/30, "The playbook, and AGENTS.md as a pointer").
  The audit also found two open owner calls that were recorded only in docs/23's prose and in the
  project chat, now docs/33 items 11 (antibiotic loot weight) and 12 (a held colonist striking its
  holder). It found docs/37's throughput trap still pricing a day at 288,000 ticks, the four-hour
  day, which is fixed to 72,000. Gates: `npm run check:routing` (the new routing-row paths and
  scripts resolve) and `npm run format:check`. No game behaviour, sim code, gate, content or
  workflow changed.

- **Needs — every colonist starts with a bottle, 2026-10-22 (the owner's pick on the water
  card).** The player, Mara and Ellis each boot carrying one `item.water.bottle.empty`: the uniques
  in their content `kit`, the player from `SimBoot.playable` beside the annex knife. The well verb
  stays. Gate: `godot:m2:needs` BOTTLE, three colonists with one bottle each, a unique's Water job
  targeting the bottle it carries and the full player at the well offered the fill, both offers gone
  with every empty taken away; run red against main first. Three pocket fixtures that assumed empty
  pockets now take the boot bottle away first (`godot:m2:comfort` MENU, `godot:check:loot`'s
  take-from and take-all lanes, `godot:m2:jobs`' two Water lanes). Measured, ten days, three seeds,
  wipe day 20260805 / 31337 / 404: 4 / 8 / 9 on main bbb4a46, 7 / 3 / 1 with the bottles; what that
  does and does not show is in "Balance after the alpha" above, and the tables are report-noise.md
  in the project's planning/balance folder.

- **Needs — water at the well, 2026-10-21 (alpha A24 follow-up).** The owner's water question
  (docs/33), answered by the card's default: E at a water source drinks while a full drink fits and
  then fills a carried empty bottle (`SimNeeds.well_offer`, `use_well`; the `well` rung of
  `SimFortify.rung_of`; the right-click menu carries the same row), and tops up only while half a
  drink still lands. Raw water is the untreated
  bottle's `drink` block, illness included. The scripted survivor uses it when nothing drinkable
  is carried or stocked. Gate: `godot:m2:needs` WELL, through the real E command on a booted
  district's well, with true negatives for a survivor past the half-drink floor with nothing to fill and one four
  metres off, and forty mouthfuls that make some ill and not all. Before it the colony's water
  was the A24 defect "no water that lasts ten days": the Water job needed an empty bottle, the
  player had no verb at the well, and after the building-noise and idle-colonist PRs the last
  survivor on seeds 31337 and 404 died of thirst on day 6. Ten-day numbers with the well are in
  report-noise.md in the project's planning/balance folder. Not built: the card's other two
  levers (a starting empty bottle, more water in the loot).

- **Balance — an idle colonist walks home from a zombie, 2026-10-21 (alpha A24 follow-up).**
  The third way into the push loop the building-noise pass found (a grab, a break-away, a stop
  inside reach and a re-grab, each break-away 2.7 m further from home). Seed 31337's c80 was
  dirty with no water to wash in, so the hygiene seek claimed every tick and did nothing; they
  stood at the annex door with no job until a zombie took them and herded them 150 tiles into a
  corner. One commit, three rules in `SimJobs._tick_one`, each with a lane that fails on the old
  `jobs.gd` and its true negative in `godot:m2:jobs`:
  - **IDLE:** a colonist outside the annex with a zombie within `DANGER_METRES` walks home
    whatever they were doing, not only on an errand (`_exposed_idle`; Guard, an order, a Retreat
    already under way and a running channel are exempt).
  - **RETREAT-SEEK:** a walk home is not dropped for a need that can wait; an empty pool or the
    far end of a band (`_hard_seek`) still outranks it.
  - **WASH:** a wash with nothing to wash in (`_can_wash`) no longer takes the tick.

  **Measured, three seeds:** a three-day check kept all three colonies alive at day 3, where the
  building-noise head lost 20260805's colony by day 4. Ten-day runs on this head are in flight;
  the numbers go in report-noise.md in the project's planning/balance folder, and here.
  The scripted survivor is still pushed the same way (20260805's successor, c94, to (189, 38) on
  day 1): that is the bot's own fight-or-flee, outside the colony's rules.

- **Balance — the building-noise pass, 2026-10-21 (alpha A24 follow-up).** Four commits, each
  with its before and after on the A24 driver (`npm run godot:playtest`):
  - **Construction noise 30 to 15** (`SimFortify.CONSTRUCT_NOISE`, docs/03, docs/30). Zombies
    within 15 m of the annex at tick 12,000: 7 to 2 on seed 31337, 4 to 1 on 20260805, 1 to 2
    either way on 404. Alone it saved no seed: 20260805, 31337 and 404 wiped on days 4, 1 and 2.
  - **Self-aid waits for no zombie within `RELEASE_METRES`** (R10, docs/30). A freed colonist
    knelt 2 m from a zombie still chasing them and was re-taken; sixty cycles on 31337 pushed one
    60 tiles from home. Seed 404 went from wiped on day 2 to all three alive through day 2, bites
    on day 1 107 to 20. Gates: `godot:m2:contact` FLIGHT-CANCELS-PRESS (no press while the holder
    is near, re-grab later than the cooldown, the press re-opening under the hold) with
    BREAKAWAY-DEFER the positive; `godot:m2:tick` CLAW at the new radius.
  - **Doctor skips a patient with a zombie within `DANGER_TARGET_METRES`**, Haul's rule.
    `godot:m2:jobs` DANGER.
  - **The balance gate's "packet on a gate" was a colonist rising at home.** `_placed_since`
    skips bodies with `turnedFrom`; the PLACED lane holds a zombie on the gate as one illegal
    placement and the same body risen from a colonist as none. The A24 defect "the director can
    place a packet on a gate" is answered by this: the director never did.

  **Measured, three seeds:** main (A24 final) wiped on days 9, 2 and 2 (20260805, 31337, 404).
  With all four commits: 20260805 wiped day 4 (the scripted survivor's successor pushed 150 tiles
  on day 1, the last colonist turned),
  31337 and 404 one alive at the end of day 5 on ten-day runs of the merged head (still running
  when this was written). The day 10 target on 2 of 3 seeds is **not** met by this pass: the
  third way into the push loop, an idle colonist, is the entry above. The report and raw logs are
  in the project's planning/balance folder as report-noise.md.

- **Balance — the A24 pass: a ten-day playtest driver, and what it found, 2026-10-21 (alpha
  A24).** The measuring half shipped and the tuning half did not move the outcome. What landed:
  - **The driver**, `godot/playtest/ten_day.gd` (`npm run godot:playtest`): the shipped 256-tile
    district, one scripted survivor (fight what is in reach, hold or back off from a crowd, loot
    the nearest unguarded container or ground item within 70 tiles, eat, drink, sleep in the
    bed, give up on a zombie it cannot reach), ten days, a line per day (food, water, wounds,
    infection, bites, kills, deaths and who, headcount, tick mean/p95/worst) and a JSON log. A
    day ran 8 to 20 minutes of wall time on the loaded session machine.
  - **Seven fixes, each its own commit with its before and after:** the player never woke from
    a bed (`SimNeeds.wake`, `godot:m2:needs` WAKE); a bite took 60 to 72 in-game days to turn
    (the owner's "Bite in days", docs/30; `godot:m2:lethality` and the infection gates); an
    errand broke off from nothing (`SimJobs.BREAK_OFF_FROM_DANGER`: a colonist out on Haul,
    Scavenge, Water, Bury, Dress, Rearm or Doctor with a zombie inside 6 m walks home and waits
    600 ticks, and Haul and Scavenge refuse a target with one inside 10 m; `godot:m2:jobs`
    DANGER); Haul, Scavenge, Doctor and Bury reached 40 tiles out, so colonists died 80 to 130
    tiles from home (`SimJobs.ERRAND_RADIUS_TILES` 20, HOME_RADIUS_TILES still 40 for Dress,
    Rearm and the guard; ERRAND); the latrine was sited by map distance and was a 54-step walk
    through the street from the start, now 19 (`SimBoot._latrine_by_route`); a colonist's thirst
    seek took only bottled water, so soda and tea on the pile were never drunk (WATER).
  - **Three gate lanes** leaned on the old colony and now judge their own system: dormant
    ASLEEP and settlers FIGHTS clear the colony (its building noise woke and called off their
    probes), storm WORK pins the radius and the danger rule.

  **Measured, same driver, main 2e920b3 against the final head, three seeds:**

  | Seed | Baseline | Final |
  |---|---|---|
  | 20260805 | colonist dead on Haul 132 tiles out day 1, one of thirst day 6, player day 7: wiped day 7 | all three alive to day 4, one of thirst day 6, player day 7: wiped day 9 |
  | 31337 | player dead 130 tiles out day 1, colonist on the latrine walk day 2, sepsis day 4: wiped day 4 | guard and player killed at home by the first night's crowd: wiped day 2 |
  | 404 | doctor dead 83 tiles out and player 102 tiles out on day 1, last colonist alive to day 10 | both colonists dead on a Dress loop day 1, player day 2: wiped day 2 |

  Colonist-days alive (headcount at each day's end, summed): 24 baseline, 19 final. The far
  deaths are gone; what kills now is the crowd the colony's own building draws to the door,
  the armour walk and thirst (each on the defect list with its numbers).
  `godot:m2:balance` stayed green through every commit kept, so its expectations did not move;
  its FAST lines did (20260805 3/3 to 2/3 survivors, the armour cut 28.7% to 24.1%). **Not
  shipped:** refusing guarded armour and weapons in Dress and Rearm fixed seed 404 in the
  playtest (headcount 2 through day 3) and lost the FAST campaign's seed 404 (0/3), so it was
  reverted; the loop is on the defect list. The report, with the raw logs, is in the project's
  planning/balance folder.

- **UI overhaul, slice 1: one bar, care on the figure, the field HUD in the locker, 2026-10-20
  (alpha A20).** Taken from docs/32's own order: the first bullet of [the UI overhaul
  group](#ui-overhaul), less the storage half #153 already landed. What changed, all under
  `godot/ui/` and the two coordinator files:
  - **One navigation bar** (`ui/nav_bar.gd`). Survivor, Colony and Skills are tabs with their keys
    on them. Tab, J and K switch in one press and put the screen in front away. The bar names who
    is being looked at, stamped "you", "viewing" or (on Colony) "everyone", and ends in the kit's
    close glyph. The sheet draws the same bar in its own title strip. Over Colony and Skills the
    bar stands alone above the locker's wash, and `main.gd`'s `_show_screen` keeps exactly one
    screen up.
  - **Escape and the HUD.** Escape puts away the one thing in front. On the sheet that is a drag,
    then the item menu, then a picked part, then the sheet. Before, Escape on the sheet or the
    work grid also raised the settings sheet over it. The field HUD is put away under all three
    screens, and the street's belt strip under Colony and Skills (the sheet keeps its own belt
    row); the work grid and the web used to draw over a lit HUD.
  - **Care on the figure** (`ui/care_pane.gd`). A click on a region of the existing figure picks
    it: an amber ring on the figure, and the inspect slot shows the part's state words, wound
    notes and a care row. The figure's hit test reads the same painted chart the figure draws.
    The care row comes from `SimTreatment.options_for`, the dry run behind command validation:
    an offered verb is a button that pushes `treat.begin`, a refused one says why in words (no
    dressing on you, stop the bleeding first), and a running treatment offers only "stop"
    (`treat.cancel`). No new treatment rule lives in the interface. The list above gives up rows
    to the pane until every refusal fits, and a refusal too wide for the pane wraps rather than
    losing its reason. The figure's panel is taped "worn", so it no longer repeats the tab.
  - **The field HUD's cards, tip and action bar wear the Salvage Locker** (near-opaque steel,
    tape label, rivets), so the street and the sheet are one kit, and the street's figure sits on
    a locker card. The action bar names the three screens in one token, "Tab J K screens", so
    every key still fits at 1280×720 beside an E clause; the F1 legend names each.
  - **The skill web wears the locker too**, with a tape label that no longer repeats whose web it
    is (the bar says that), and follows the bar when a colonist is picked while it is up. As a
    stopgap it is centred under the bar and, on a window shorter than its natural size, the web
    between its words shrinks to fit: at 1280×720 every node, region word and the footer are on
    screen. Labels that already crowded each other still do; the reflow is the second bullet's.

  **Not changed:** the sim, the read models, the figure's art, the Colony and Skills screens' own
  contents, the bans. **Evidence:** `godot:check:play`'s new NAV lane, in the real scene at
  1280×720: a key walk round all three screens with one screen up, the HUD dark and the belt
  strip put away under each. A click on the bar's free room does nothing, a tab click switches,
  close goes to the street and the sheet's own Skills tab reaches Skills. Escape on Colony opens
  no settings, and on the sheet with a part picked it puts the part down and stops there. The
  street's swing stays refused under the two new focuses. `godot:check:inventory`'s new CARE
  lane picks a cut arm at the figure's own point and offers exactly what `options_for` says
  works, every refusal in words. A press on hold pressure queues the one `treat.begin`, a
  dressing in the bag makes "dress it" offered, and Escape puts the part down. Its negative is a
  part with no wound, which offers nothing. `check_ui_skin`'s GLYPHS lane now finds the close
  glyph's reader in `nav_bar.gd`. `check_shots` gains the care and skills scenes (seven now),
  set up at 1280×720. `godot:check:play`, `:inventory`, `:hud`, `:respond`, `:appearance`,
  `:context`, `:web_look`, `:speech`, `:memory`, `:ui_skin`, `:shots`, `godot:ban:healthbar`,
  `godot:smoke`, `godot:validate`, `check:routing` and `npm test` pass locally. The NAV lane also
  holds the bar and the web to the same person (you, then a colonist "viewing") and the web
  inside the 1280×720 window; `godot:check:hud`'s new BAR lane holds the hint to every key at
  1280×720 beside the trip-alarm clause, its negative a hint one token too long; the CARE lane's
  FIT holds a refusal whole in a narrow pane. `check_shots` gains colony and viewing (nine
  scenes). Before and after shots at both windows are in the project's planning files under
  ui-slice-1, reviewed once by the art QA pass. **Not shown or proven:** a treatment run to its
  end from the pane, a colonist treated from the pane, the Colony grid's own look (still the old
  kit), and the speech bubble's style (both the second bullet's).

  **Second review round, on the 2 px art grid.** The art QA pass measured the shots and the
  fixes landed on this entry. Every locker outline is now inset 2 px fills
  (`Locker.rim`) instead of a centred stroke, so the care pane's buttons, the active tab and
  the chips start and end on even pixels; the care button's row is snapped to the grid. Text
  sits on whole multiples of VT323's pixel: the tab words at 4x on a tall window and 2x on a
  short one, the care pane's part heading at 2x. The figure on the sheet scales by an even
  whole number and sits on an even pixel, so at 1920×1080 it is 2x where it was 3x and the
  picked part's ring no longer has odd edges. The skill web keeps its full width at 1280×720
  and only its height gives way, its discs sit on even centres and radii, and a label plan tries
  each name (with a keystone's price) on its home side, then the other, a row or two up or down,
  keeping 8 px of ink from every other word and off every other disc, so at 1280×720 no name
  sits on another or under a node; `godot:check:web_look`'s new CROWD lane holds that at both
  sizes, and its negative is the short web with every name on its home row, which crowds. Its locked ink is raised to (142,136,126), above 4.5:1 on
  the steel, and its footer legend wraps to two lines instead of ending in "…". The Colony
  grid sizes each column to its own head plus a 20 px gap and stands against the panel's right
  edge, so the heads ("Construct") and the taglines get the width the grid used to leave empty,
  and Scavenge no longer runs into Water; `godot:check:play`'s WORK-LAYOUT lane holds both, at
  1280×720 and 1920×1080, against the edges the click math reads. The street's figure card
  lines up with the belt at x 16 and carries a "body" tape like every other HUD card.
  **Third round.** The web's discs, keystone rings and hub dot are drawn in whole 2×2 art
  pixels (`web_panel.gd`'s `_blocks`) instead of smooth circles whose 2 px rings landed on odd
  edges, and its lines are 2 px moved half their width onto even columns;
  `godot:check:web_look`'s CROWD lane now also holds every disc's box and art pixels to the
  even grid, refusing the odd box the review measured. Locked ink is (146,140,130), 4.5:1 even
  on the steel's lighter streak. A "you" card tall enough to reach the street's body card
  starts right of it and runs down beside the figure, not over it; one that ends above the body
  card stays at the margin, so at 1920×1080 it does not hang beside an empty strip. The body
  card ends 4 px short of the action bar. `godot:check:play`'s HUD-CARDS lane holds all of it at
  1280×720 and 1920×1080 with a one-line and a five-line "you" card, its negative the five-line
  card with no body card to make room for, which overlaps at 1280×720.
  **Left for slice 2**, from this slice: the web's dashed lines can start on an odd row, its
  diagonal lines step a pixel per row rather than in 2×2 blocks, and the region circle's rim is
  1 px. Each also on main before this slice: VT323's 1 px glyph bearing, which
  starts the bar's words and the care pane's text a pixel off the grid; the figure's wound dot
  (a 1 px red rim) and its smooth ground shadow; the keycaps' 1 px outlines and
  corner steps; text that is not on a whole VT323 multiple (the HUD's "You" and OUTSIDE lines,
  the tip card, the interior action bar's shrunk labels, the bar's hint and stamps, the web's
  labels); the inventory's filter chips and the equipped-knife slot off the grid; the interior
  camera's odd offset; and the bark bubble's old green style and clipped first glyph.

- **UI — the inventory, redone (the Salvage Locker), 2026-10-19.** The owner's answer to the
  alpha plan's Q5: keep the grid, which reads like Tarkov's, but it "looks very plain" and has to
  look bespoke; and a fast list beside it with the grid still the authority on capacity. Three
  directions were drawn at 1920×1080 with the repo's own icons (canvas webbing, a salvage locker,
  a hard case); the locker was built, and the owner confirmed it on 2026-10-20 (docs/30, "The
  inventory's look"). What changed, all
  under `godot/ui/`: a new `locker.gd` skin (brushed steel, rivets, masking-tape labels,
  recessed cells, plates tinted by item class with a dog-ear, amber selection brackets, rust
  hazard stripes for a refused drop) replaces the kit frames on the inventory's surfaces; a bag
  cell is 60 px — thirty art pixels at the world's 2× — so an item's 32 px picture sits in one
  cell at the size the same thing has on the floor, and `ItemPicture.draw` crops to the painted
  part and lays a long gun along its footprint; the sheet gains a title bar (with the kit's close
  glyph, now read), a list of everything in reach with six kind chips that fade the grids rather
  than hide cells, a ctrl-click that sends an item to the box you stand at or back into the
  first bag with room (cell by cell through `SimInventory.can_place`, then `item.move` through the
  queue), and verb buttons along the inspect pane's foot drawn from the same rects the press is
  tested against. The quick strip and the item menu (and so the street's right-click menu, which
  draws through it) wear the same skin. The transfer window now clears the action bar where the
  screen is tall enough for both. `Chrome.item_plate` lost its last caller and was removed.
  **Not changed:** the sim, the read models, the digit and health-bar bans, the one typeface,
  the column order, the 1280 two-lane rule. **Against docs/32**, which recommends flatter
  surfaces and a sans body face: the owner's "super awesome, bespoke" ask and the locker pick
  settle the inventory's surfaces; the face stays VT323 as the current baseline, because
  typography is still one of docs/32's open recommendations and this slice does not decide it.

  **Evidence:** `godot:check:inventory`'s new QUICK lane drives real presses in a 1920×1080
  SubViewport: the list carries every item the grids do and only weapons under the arms chip
  (pressed, not set), a row press selects; a ctrl-press moves the bottle into the open cupboard
  after a step and pushes nothing with the box closed; the pane's drop button drops the knife
  and a miss pushes nothing. Sabotaging the ctrl-press and the button's `_act` turns SEND and
  BUTTONS red. Gate edits, each deliberate: `check_appearance`'s shared-draw needle reads
  `draw_texture_rect_region(` (the crop), `check_ui_skin`'s CURSORS needle reads `Locker.refuse(`
  for the refusal, PANEL drops `item_plate`, and GLYPHS moves `glyph_close` from unused to a
  reader. `godot:check:inventory`, `:ui_skin`, `:appearance`, `:respond`, `:context`, `:hud`,
  `:play`, `godot:ban:healthbar` and `godot:smoke` pass locally; the full chain passed in CI.
  [Before/after captures](../.hermes/plans/2026-10-19_inventory-redesign/README.md) at 1280×720
  and 1920×1080 from one throwaway driver (deleted). Not shown or proven: a drag in flight, the
  ghost and the stripes on screen, a human using the list in a real run; and at 1280 with a box
  open the inspect pane gives way to the two lanes, so its buttons are not on screen there.

- **Gate infrastructure — the `godot:m2` chain runs as four CI shards, 2026-10-19.** The
  85-gate chain took 40m45s on one runner (job 118220307956, measured on 2b48fef), against the
  45-minute `godot-m2` limit. `scripts/m2-shards.mjs` splits it into four `godot-m2-shard` jobs,
  balanced by those per-gate times; `godot:m2:balance` alone (791 s) is the floor on wall time.
  `godot-m2` is now the aggregate required check and fails unless every shard passed. The gates
  that write the per-machine `user://` store share shard 3. `npm run check:shards` (`SHARDS_OK`;
  its self-test refuses five broken layouts) proves each chained gate is in exactly one shard.
  Unsharded `npm run godot:m2` is unchanged. Wall time of the sharded run: see the PR.
- **UI — the small fixes of alpha A22, 2026-10-19.** O cycles off and light. The noise, scent and
  sight channels were never drawn (`godot:check:light`'s O-key rider), so they are dropped rather
  than drawn; drawing them is a later slice if the owner wants it. M, the raw developer sheets, and
  F8, the spawn menu, act only in a debug build: the router guards M the way it guards F8, the HUD
  names M only in a debug build, and the legend lists neither. `godot:check:play`'s SOCKET lane
  checks both guards in source, and its KEYS lane excuses M by name in UNLISTED. The guards are read
  from source, so the gate proves the check is in front of the key, not how a release binary
  behaves. A waiting recruit in reach offers "turn them away", which sends them through the sim's own
  `recruit.ignore`; `godot:check:context`'s DECLINE lane proves the row is offered in reach, absent
  out of reach and for a body that is not waiting, and that dispatching it removes the recruit.
- **UI — the work grid draws only the columns something does, 2026-10-19 (alpha A15).**
  `ui/work_panel.gd`'s `shown_columns` draws the twelve job columns that have a consumer
  (`SimJobs.CONSUMERS`), in the sim's order, and no others: the six stubs (Firefight, Hunt, Farm,
  Craft, Modify, Butcher) are gone from the grid. The sim still stores their numbers and nothing
  reads them. Dropping them from `SimJobs.COLUMNS` would change the job row, presets and saves, so
  that is a sim change and is not taken here. `godot:check:play`'s STUBS lane proves the grid's list
  equals the consumers, names no stub, and that its first cell queues the first column it draws;
  with the filter set to draw everything, that lane goes red.
- **Art — the night, per pixel, 2026-10-19.** Item A10 of the 2026-10-19 alpha plan, built on
  the baked world (A4), revised twice after the coordinator's art reviews (2026-10-20). The night
  was one flat navy fill whose alpha came from the survivor's own sight, warm pools were per-tile
  rects under the bodies, and the edge of sight was the shadowcast's tiles stepping straight into
  a navy void. Now `presentation/light_map.gd` draws one screen rect multiplied over everything
  main draws (`night_light.gdshader`, `blend_mul`, so it can only darken) and a glow item over it
  for the flash and the flame. Where light may land is the sim's: the per-source "does this cast
  reach this tile and does the survivor see it" answer is handed over as bits
  (`LightLook.light_texels`), so a wall stops light on screen exactly where it stops it in the
  sim, and a source's light fades over the inner half of the last tile it holds to nothing at
  the edge of every neighbour it does not hold, corners included, never onto a tile the survivor
  does not see. How much light lands is the look: each
  source draws a pool out to 0.3 of its sim reach and nothing past it, in five flat rings with an
  ordered dither only in the band between two (`LightLook.POOL_LEVELS`), at a brightness capped
  by its reach (`LightLook.source_cap`: a 20 m campfire 0.85 of daylight, a 16 m storm lantern
  0.75). The campfire's content tint is a redder orange (`#ff9452`) and the oil lanterns a
  yellower one (`#ffdf80`), so two overlapping pools read as two. Outside every pool the night
  holds at the floor of the unseen dark: at midnight full dark is `LightLook.NIGHT_FLOOR` (0.24)
  of the night's colour, no channel above 8 of 255 even on a white tile. The survivor's
  own disc of ground (`EYE_FLOOR` 0.55, ringed the same way) ends half a tile inside their sight
  radius (`LightLook.eye_disc_metres`), so it is round rather than cut by the plus of tiles a
  1.9 m night sight sees. The edge of sight is softened across the tile boundary, half a tile
  into each side, and dithered. The void (never seen, drawn by no layer, R 0 in the texels where
  a remembered tile is 128) cannot be faded by a multiply, so the known map's last half tile
  beside it walks down to the void's dark instead. A window's light is still per tile: the cast
  through it fades to nothing at the window row's edges, so its band on the far side peaks at
  the pane and the masonry above and below it stays nearly dark, but the pane's own outline is
  not traced. Light passes a window onto the floor beyond and not onto the masonry there: the
  sim's shadowcast lights the first opaque tile it meets through glass (a hedge or a shelf whose
  picture reads as the wall going on), so the screen lights an opaque tile only from a source
  that also lights one of its four open neighbours (anything not blocking sight except glass),
  the ground its face looks onto (`LightLook._face_lit`; art review 3). Deep water is solid but
  clear, so it is not filtered: the middle of a pond stays lit. The window's own glass fades
  toward the dark masonry behind it, as every lit tile fades toward an unlit neighbour. By day the light map is cleared, not drawn, so the day frame is the one it
  was before (pixel-identical at both sizes). Everything is evaluated on the 32 px art-pixel
  grid. Flames (a campfire, oil, a candle) flicker by at most 3% of reach, only ever down; cells
  and gas are steady. A torch, headlamp or weapon light draws as a beam along its carrier's
  facing: content's new `light.beam` half-angle, presentation only. The tile pools under the
  bodies are now the O channel's alone. Looks chosen without the owner, each the default
  nearest Zero Sievert: flames flicker, a torch is a wedge; full night near black is the owner's
  pick on the darkness card (2026-10-20). **Half shipped, and which half:** the sim still lights
  a torch's whole round cast, and outside the beam the screen draws only a disc at the hand, so
  a zombie still reads the light behind you; the sim cone and its attention cost are the torch
  piece in what's left. And the screen now draws less light than the sim in two places named
  there as "The night's reach on screen": a campfire's sim cast is 20 m and its pool 6 m, and a
  survivor's unlit night sight is 1.9 m, which bounds the disc.

  **Evidence:** `npm run godot:check:light` → `LIGHT_LOOK_OK`. NO LIGHT ON UNSEEN (the plan's
  lane): a campfire behind a wall lights 288 tiles in the sim that the survivor does not see,
  and every one is four zero bytes in the light map. Every source bit sits on a seen tile, and
  the open twin's same tile is seen and carries its bit. A builder that writes bits before the
  seen test was run as sabotage and went red. After the survivor walks away, every tile reads R
  128 exactly where it is remembered and not seen, and 0 for the void. RINGS: four or five
  rings; the midnight floor keeps every channel at 8 or under; `source_cap` keeps its
  ends and is monotonic; the campfire caps above the storm lantern and its tint is redder; the
  dark eye disc is the sky's share of the range and there is none with nobody to ask.
  SIGHT-DERIVED now judges the eye disc: a campfire a metre away widens it from 1.92 m to its
  3.5 m cap. DAYLIGHT: at noon `ambient_of` is 1 and `_draw_night_wash` clears the light map
  before it builds one. BEAM: a carried hand torch is its content's 22° along the facing; no
  facing and a lantern are round; every content beam can be carried. FLICKER: a campfire
  flickers, a cell torch does not. DEAD SOCKET is re-pointed: the night is built from
  `light_texels`, `ambient_of` and `eye_disc_metres` before `_draw_effects(true)`, which blits
  into the glow item; `light_map.gd` hands the shader the caps, rings, eye floor and disc; and
  the shader rings every light and lights only seen tiles. The per-point fraction and curve
  helpers the first cut drew from (`light_fraction_at`, `shown`, `wash_alpha`) went with the look
  that read them, and their lanes with them. `godot:check:appearance` pins the campfire's new
  tint. Budget: see docs/22's light-map section. **2026-10-24 (night draw, B1):** the committed
  `night-draw` sample (`godot:bench:frame`, `check:runtime-budget`) measures the night at the day's
  draw on llvmpipe, median 10.0 ms against 13.9 ms; the texels are cached per tick and the light
  texture uploads only when they change, and night screenshots are pixel-identical. Numbers in docs/22. Before, first-cut and revised shots are in the
  project's `planning/lighting/`, with an overlap shot and a torch aimed point-blank at a wall
  with two windows: light passes the windows and stops at the masonry between them. WINDOW: a
  campfire inside a room lights a screen tile behind the glass in the sim, and it carries no
  source bit; the floor beyond the same glass, the wall's room-side face, a screen beside that
  lit floor and the middle of a pond keep theirs. With the refusal switched off the lane went
  red, and so did the first cut of the rule, which filtered every solid tile and so darkened the
  pond.

- **The torch on screen, 2026-10-24.** Slice B3 of the three-features plan, after the sim's cone
  (B2, docs/30's "The torch is a cone"). The light map's bits for a beam are the sim's own:
  `LightLook.light_texels` asks `SimLight.lights_tile` for every seen tile in view, so a hand
  torch lights the tiles ahead in its wedge and the spill at its back, and the tiles behind it
  past the spill carry no bit though its round cast reaches them. `source_beam` and the facing
  are read off the light index (`source_at`), not content. The beam leaves the hand that holds
  the light (`LightLook.hand_metres`: the slot's hand off the feet-anchored pawn canvas, on the
  frame the body was drawn on; seen from behind, the hand's side on the ground under the body, so
  the beam does not read as a headlamp), and a headlamp, in no hand, leaves the body's point. The
  disc at the hand is `SimLight.SPILL_M`, handed to the shader as `spill_m`. Two sim calls came with it
  (docs/30, "The torch on screen"): a beam lights every tile it falls on, within `BEAM_EDGE_M`
  (1 m) of its edge, so the drawn beam keeps straight edges inside the lit tiles instead of the
  tile-centre staircase the first cut drew; and a carrier with no facing throws round, as the B2
  plan said and the light index did not. Where a beam crosses a round pool the brighter sets the
  level and the colour is the two tints weighed by brightness, so a torch over a campfire's ground
  stays warm, with no channel above what the brighter light gives alone; a pixel only one light
  reaches keeps its tint exactly (the torch shots are pixel-identical to before). New review scene `night_torch`: midnight on an open
  street, a hand torch down the longest east-west run, a shambler 5 m into the beam and one 5 m
  behind in the dark.

  **Evidence:** `npm run godot:check:light` → `LIGHT_LOOK_OK`. BEAM is re-pointed, not loosened:
  the torch's beam on screen equals the sim's and the content's 22°; on a tile 6 m ahead, the
  spill tile behind and a tile 6 m behind, all seen, the bit equals `lights_tile` (present, present,
  absent) though the round cast reaches the third; a storm lantern's bit is on that tile; a carrier
  with no facing is round in the sim and on screen; the torch leaves the secondary hand
  (-0.14, -0.25 m off the feet at zoom 64) and a headlamp the body's point. DEAD SOCKET adds
  `LightLook.hand_metres` in `_draw_night_wash`, `SimLight.SPILL_M` in `light_map.gd` and the
  shader's spill disc and inward edge. `npm run godot:m2:torch` → `M2_TORCH_OK`: CONE adds the
  tile the beam's edge crosses (27° off at 4.5 m, lit) and the no-facing carrier (round); READS
  no longer skips: the light map lights 6 m ahead and not 6 m behind. Each was run red by
  sabotage: texels asking the round cast (BEAM, READS), no edge margin (CONE), a beam kept with no
  facing (CONE, BEAM), the hand origin zeroed (BEAM), the spill not handed to the shader and a
  beam's tint replacing a pool's (DEAD SOCKET). `npm run godot:check:shots` → `SHOTS_OK` with
  seventeen scenes (sixteen on main's C4 head, plus `night_torch`); NEGATIVE refuses a day street
  and the torchless night as the torch shot. Before and after shots of `night_lights` and
  `night_torch` at both windows, and the first cut's staircase, are in the project's
  `planning/night-torch/`. Art QA on the beam's origin and the disc. Frame cost, the committed
  `night-draw` sample (a hand torch and a campfire), three interleaved runs each on llvmpipe:
  branch 11.45, 10.62, 11.17 ms mean (median 11.17), main 10.75, 10.24, 11.36 (median 10.75),
  inside the run-to-run noise of about 1 ms. Main's night draw is itself over its 10 ms target
  on this container; that is B1's open number, not this slice's.
  A campfire's flicker follows the shader's real-time clock (`TIME` in `night_light.gdshader`),
  so a shot with a fire in it is not pixel-stable between runs (about 20k pixels at 1080p in the
  torch-over-campfire shot). A before/after pixel diff of such a shot pins the time first, or
  compares only shots with no flame in view; the plain `night_torch` scene has none and is stable.

- **Art — the overcast day, 2026-10-24 (three-features plan, B5).** The day half of docs/30's
  "Overcast or torchlight", as docs/30's "The overcast day, as a grade" records it: a pass over the
  finished picture, not a palette regrade, because most of the screen is the outpost pack's art and
  no palette entry reaches it. **The grade** is `presentation/day_grade.gd` and
  `day_grade.gdshader`, one RenderingServer rect at draw index 998 under main's canvas item, under
  the night's multiply (1000) and its glow (1001) and under the HUD's CanvasLayer. By day it pulls
  each pixel toward its own grey (keeps 68% of its colour in the lit middle, 20% in the darks),
  cools it (red 0.97, blue 1.03) and veils it 10% toward #5c5e60. Its weight is
  `smoothstep(NIGHT_AMBIENT, 1, ambient)`: 1 by day, 0.5 at mid-dusk, 0 at night, when it draws
  nothing. At mid-dusk the night's multiply already holds the frame and the grey shift is barely
  measurable (`dusk_street` chroma 6.2 → 6.4 at 1280×720, 7.3 → 7.0 at 1920×1080, the art review's
  numbers). The void goes from #15141f to #1c1c20 by day. `main.gd`'s `_draw_day_grade` drives it,
  called in `_draw` before `_draw_night_wash`. **The world's words are never graded:** the speech
  bubbles and the pawn tag are recorded in `_world_text_ops` during `_draw` and painted by
  `_paint_world_text` on a child item, `_world_text`, at draw index 999 (`DayGrade.TEXT_INDEX`),
  over the grade and under the night, which still dims them as before; `godot:check:ui_skin`'s
  OUTLIERS lane follows the plate's `Chrome.frame(` to `_paint_world_text`, re-pointed with its
  commented-call negative, not loosened. **A zombie's sound-word is
  lifted** from `Chrome.TEXT_DIM` 40% toward `Chrome.TEXT` (`main.gd`'s `bubble_ink`), from 3.34:1
  to 4.89:1 on its plate over the brightest ground, still quieter than speech (art review round 1).
  **The stockpile's rims hold 3:1 under the grade:** measured in the graded picture, the rest rim

  lighter amber rim (`STOCKPILE_ADD_RIM` #e6b158) and the clear rim is lighter (#f2a185);
  `godot:check:memory`'s STOCKPILE lane holds every rim at 3:1 through `DayGrade.grade` (worst
  3.10:1 graded, 3.49:1 in source colours), red at the old three values, and refuses a graded
  measure the grade lowers nowhere. **A new review scene,** `dusk_street`: the day street's spot
  at mid-dusk (`Scenes.DUSK` 0.6875), the last of `check_shots.gd`'s NAMES; and the shot driver runs at a fixed frame step
  (`--fixed-fps 60` in `scripts/run-godot.mjs`'s `--shots` mode), so shader time and a flame's
  flicker are the same at every capture. **The gate** is new, `npm run godot:check:grade`
  (`godot/check_grade_look.gd`, `GRADE_LOOK_OK`): PHASE (1 at noon, 0 at midnight, 0.5 at
  mid-dusk, rising through dawn), DAY (fourteen palette entries through the grade pinned to a
  measured table, each source colour and the weight-0 answer refused by its pin; 23 warm entries

- **Feel — bodies glide between ticks, and a slow frame drops time, 2026-10-19.** Item A2 of
  the 2026-10-19 alpha plan. The sim steps at 20 Hz and every body used to be drawn on the
  position component, so a walker held still for a tick and then jumped a tick's travel at
  once, however fast the frames came. `presentation/interp.gd` (`RenderInterp`) snapshots each
  drawn body's position and facing just before every `world.step()`, and `_draw_entities` draws
  at `lerp(previous tick, current tick, accumulator / TICK_SECONDS)`: one tick of render delay,
  traded for motion that never jumps. Riders slide with the vehicle they ride, a live vehicle's
  picture with its entity, the facing line and aim cone (both retired by A9, below; the aim now
  glides the same way) turn the short way between ticks, and a
  jump past `SNAP_METRES` (4 m in one tick: a load, a mount, a reused id) draws on the new point
  at once. The camera now follows the drawn point and updates after the frame's ticks rather
  than before them, so it no longer chases a target that steps. `_process` clamps its
  accumulator to the per-frame cap (`RenderInterp.clamp_debt`): a hitch used to leave seconds of
  debt that every later frame paid at the cap; now the time past the cap is dropped. The rain
  reads the same sub-tick fraction (`_sub_tick`). Presentation only: nothing under `godot/sim/`
  changed, and sight, picking and every position a gate reads are still the component.
  **Half shipped, and which half:** the four-view pick and the walk frame still change on the
  tick (the walk frame moved to the render clock with A7, below), ground items and corpses do not move so they are not interpolated, and FX are placed at
  the sim point of the event, so a muzzle flash on a body walking at speed can sit up to one tick
  of travel ahead of it. The frame rate itself is A3/A4's work; this makes whatever rate there is
  read as motion.

  **Evidence:** `npm run godot:check:motion` → `MOTION_OK`, chained after `godot:check:camera`.
  HELPERS: `between` on the previous point at 0, the current at 1, strictly between at 0.5, snaps
  past `SNAP_METRES` and glides under it; `turn_between` turns the short way across ±π; a debt
  under the cap is left alone. CLAMP: on the real scene, a ten-second frame runs the cap of five
  ticks and leaves under one tick owed, so the next half-tick frame runs none (the old loop ran
  five more); a 75 ms frame runs one and keeps 25 ms. DRAWN: a walking player, a frame ending on
  a tick draws the body on the previous tick's point and not the current one, and a half-tick
  frame after it draws it strictly between the two on the line joining them, read back from the
  real draw's `_focal_drawn`. SMOOTH, the measurement, coefficient of variation of per-frame
  apparent speed: at a steady 60 Hz the drawn body is **0.000** against **1.414** on the tick (two
  still frames and a leap), the camera **0.036** against **0.083** for the old follow; at a
  seeded, jittered ~10 fps (60–140 ms frames, today's shipped rate) the body is **0.000** against
  **0.248** and the camera **0.051** against **0.125**. Sabotaged (`offset` returning zero) the
  gate goes red on DRAWN, both body CVs (1.414, 0.248) and both camera CVs (0.104, 0.109 against
  the 0.075 bound). READERS holds the textual half for the branches the boot does not drive: the
  snapshot before `world.step()`, the clamp before the loop, the camera after it, riders,
  vehicles and facing.

- **Feel — frames on the render clock, eight-frame walks and a breath, 2026-10-19.** Item A7 of
  the 2026-10-19 alpha plan, on A2's glide above. A walk frame used to be
  `tick * fps / 20 + id`: it moved only when a tick did, at one cadence whatever the speed, so a
  limping survivor's feet moonwalked and a sprinter's skated, and four poses a cycle read as a
  stutter. `presentation/anim_clock.gd` (`AnimClock`) now advances each drawn body's place in
  its cycle by the ground its *drawn* point covered since the last draw, so a body steps as fast
  as it is seen to move, stops stepping when it stops, and ends a path on the same frame at 30
  or at 144 frames a second. One cycle covers the family's own stride (`pace × frames / fps`, so
  a body at its family's pace steps at exactly the manifest's rate); away from that pace the
  stride lengthens with the square root of the speed, clamped to half and double, so a sprint at
  three times the pace steps about 1.7 times as often rather than three. Bodies are seated by id
  on the golden ratio so a crowd does not step as one, and a jump past `SNAP_METRES` re-seats
  rather than spinning the legs. A standing body breathes on presentation time (`delta ×
  speed`, so pause holds it and fast-forward quickens it) at the family's `breath_fps`.
  The motion a draw asks about is one Dictionary, `{walking, cycle, idle}`, read by
  `Appearance.frame_key`; it is the hook A8's action animations add a key to, and nothing here
  builds them. `main.gd` changes in `_on_world_replaced`, `_process`, `_draw`, `_draw_entities`
  and `_layer_rect` only. Presentation only: nothing under `godot/sim/` changed.

  **The art.** Every body walks on **eight frames** a view, at twice the old rate (survivor 16,
  workwear/commuter/raincoat 10, stalker 12, runner 18, armoured and heavy 8; the screamer 10
  and the bloater 8 since zombie study 02 joined on the merge of 2026-10-20, built by the same
  script from its four poses at paces 2.31 and 1.47), so the cadence on screen is unchanged and
  the motion between steps is twice as fine. The survivor's walk is
  **new generated art** -- four PixelLab strips, each animated from the pack's own rest view,
  so frame 0 is the standing picture and the old walk's skin-tone and outline pop on setting
  off is gone (the plan's "shambler palette pop" had moved to the survivor when the shambler
  was retired; it is fixed where it now lived). The **zombies' in-betweens and every breath
  are mechanical**: each family keeps its four pack poses as frames 0, 2, 4, 6, and frames 1,
  3, 5, 7 are the pose before with the rows above the hip carried one pixel toward the next
  pose's height; the breath is the rest view with the rows above the chest a pixel up (the
  survivor) or down (the dead sag, which also keeps rest views already at their canvas's
  tallest inside it). That is a row shift of the pack's pixels, not drawing, and the pack's
  `STYLE.md` asks for authored frames: **this is the half a commissioned pass should replace.**
  Built by one script, `godot/art/simplyzombies/motion/build_motion.py` (`--check` reports
  `MOTION_OK`), which also writes the pack manifests' frame lists, `authored.json`'s new
  `pace`, `breath_fps` and per-member points, and `SHA256SUMS`; sources, prompts and job ids are
  in `motion/sources/generation.json` and the method in `motion/README.md`. Five generations
  were spent: the four strips and one zombie trial that was not used.

  **Per-frame points, and the layer contract A6 builds on.** Every walk and breath member
  declares where its `head` and `torso` moved from the rest view, and the survivor's declare
  each hand. A worn layer resolves in three rules, in order: (1) the layer's own member for that
  frame, `<layer>_<frame suffix>` (`item_gear_vest_walk_e_3`), when it exists -- what A6's
  clothing will author; (2) otherwise its view picture shifted by the frame's offset for the
  region its family `rides` (`authored.json`: helmet and gas mask the head, vest and backpack the
  torso); (3) a held weapon on the frame's own hand (`Appearance.frame_hand`, falling back to
  `HELD_HANDS` at rest). A muzzle flash was still placed from the rest hand in `fx_look.gd`; A9
  (below) moved it to the hand of the frame the shooter was last drawn on.

  **The breath was the owner's call, and it is kept** (owner, 2026-10-20; docs/30's "The idle
  breath, kept"). `breath_fps: 0` in `authored.json` would turn it off per family without code.

  **Evidence:** `godot:check:worn` new FRAMES lane: **288** walk and breath frames over 8 bodies
  declare head and torso offsets the renderer reads (427 of them move one, after the art
  review's even bob; 448 before), **72** survivor hands sit on their own frame's arm (53 off the
  rest point; 57 before), and a pistol, helmet and vest on a
  walking frame follow its hand, head and torso; a corner hand, a frame-less pistol, a shifting
  rest view, a riderless wearable and a dropped frame are each refused. `godot:check:zombie_art`
  MOTION: eight distinct poses and a breath a view, stride equal to pace × frames / fps, and a
  real clock walking one stride at pace at 60 Hz reaching every frame with under 0.02 cycle
  drift. `godot:check:topdown` TURN: on the real clock, each family changes frame its manifest
  rate (±1) in a second at its pace, more but less than threefold at three times the pace, fewer
  but some at half; ids 1 and 2 seat apart; a standing second never walks. `godot:check:authored`
  holds 40 members per zombie family, eight walk and two breath frames, and the frame-name
  mapping both ways. `sprites:check` reproduces every new member from its source.

- **Feel — actions on the render clock, 2026-10-19.** Item A8 of the 2026-10-19 alpha plan, on
  A7's clock above. A body used to do nothing but walk and breathe: a shot, a blow landing, a
  stagger and a death changed no picture (a dead body cut straight to its corpse), and the
  stance was never drawn at all. Now each of those plays from what the sim already publishes or
  already holds -- `presentation/anim_clock.gd` reads `world.events.drained` (never a bus
  subscription) and the bodies' components, and `Appearance.action_key` answers the member:

  | sim source | action | who |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `weapon.fired` | recoil (2 frames) | the firer |
  | `attack.connected` | lunge (3) / flinch (3) | a zombie attacker / a living target |
  | `grab.started` | lunge | the grabbing zombie |
  | `entity.staggered` | stagger (3) / flinch | a zombie / a living body |
  | `entity.killed` | fall (2), then the settled corpse | the dead, once (de-duplicated) |
  | `swing.state` WindUp, then Recover | swing (5): the guard held, the strike thrown | survivors |
  | `rangedWeapon.state` Reload, Clearing | reload (8), the long gun's (8) or the shotgun's (8), held on the stance | survivors |
  | `posture.current` Crouch, Crawl | crouch (1) and crouched walk (8); the crawl (8) | survivors |

  A one-shot wins over a stance, a body lying down plays nothing upright, and the crawl lies
  across the screen (east or west, the side it last faced) carrying no worn or held layer.
  Times are presentation seconds, so pause holds an action and fast-forward quickens it.
  The survivor family is every pack human (player, colonists, raiders); every zombie pose family
  carries lunge, stagger and fall, the screamer and the bloater included since zombie study 02
  made them pose families (merged in from #154 with main, 2026-10-20).
  `main.gd` changes in `_process` (one line: the drained events to the clock), `_draw_entities`
  (one line: the clock's action merged into the motion) and `_draw_corpse` (the fall, and the
  `_falls_drawn` list the gate reads). Presentation only: nothing under `godot/sim/` changed.

  **The art, and which half is which.** **496** new members (1036 since the falls landed and
  settled, the next record). **Generated: the swing's east,
  west and south views** -- three PixelLab `animate_image` strips, each from the pack's own rest
  view, five frames kept a view (`motion/sources/actions/generation.json` has the jobs, inputs,
  prompts, and the two rejected jobs). **Derived: everything else** -- the back view's swing (its
  job turned the body side-on), recoil, flinch, crouch, the crouched walk, the crawl, both
  falls, the lunge and the stagger -- by whole-pixel moves of the pack's own pictures in
  `motion/actions.py`: a lean, a dip or rise, a fold of the shins below the shorts or belt, a
  step, and for the crawl the back view's walk turned a quarter flat. No pixel is resampled or
  recoloured. **The reloads are drawn**, eight beats each for a magazine: the weapon brought in with the body
  dipping a pixel, the off hand coming under it, the magazine out (the pistol's dropped at the
  grip, the long gun's stripped from the well), the off hand to the hip as it falls, back up with
  a fresh one, seated with the body rising, the rack jolting the weapon back a pixel and forward
  again, half way home, and the stance, held while the sim's Reload lasts. Each arm the reload
  moves is taken off the rest view (`ARMLESS` closes the torso's outline where it hung) and
  drawn again as a jointed limb in the rest view's own outline and skin, so a hand goes where the
  beat sends it with a closed outline over the body: from the front over the torso, from behind
  only to the edge of the back (the hand point goes on behind it), side on the far arm under the
  body with its forearm over the belly once it reaches round; outline an arm adds is pared back
  to the pack's two pixels where it would wedge against the body's own (`_trim`). The dip and
  the rise happen at the knee (`_knee`), so the legs bend and straighten under the hips rather
  than the shorts sliding over the thighs or the waist stretching. The magazine is a 2x3 block,
  outlined, in the held pistol's gunmetal: the long gun's hangs from the off hand at hand height
  as it comes out, falls clear of the legs on the off hand's side (so the back view mirrors the
  front), and lies by the feet to the end; side on, the fresh one hangs from the fist at the
  back of the belt for a beat, below the stock, and seats with its foot showing under the well.
  From behind the long gun is held still -- not lowered with the dip, not brought in -- but for
  the rack's jolt, a pixel up: it is taller than the body there, and any travel put its muzzle
  over the head or its stock in and out of sight. A dip never rises above the stance: the body
  goes down a pixel and comes back to it. The pistol's is worked at the grip, the long gun's
  (rifle and crossbow: a held picture 48 px wide, `Appearance.reload_action`) at the well and
  fore-end five pixels along. **The shotgun is tube-fed** (`reload_tube`, for a long held
  picture whose caliber is in `TUBE_CALIBERS`, today 12-gauge): no magazine, the off hand goes
  from the belt to the loading port three times in eleven beats, a shell in the shells icon's own
  red and brass standing out of the fist at the port and pushed up into it (only its rim still
  showing) before the hand goes back for the next, so the hand is never empty and no shell
  blinks; then one rack and home, at 6 frames a second, the long guns' rate, against the sim's
  three-second Reload. The pump itself is part of A9's held picture and does not slide; the rack
  reads as the weapon jolting back in the hands. An outline an arm adds round skin the held weapon covers is taken
  back too (`_trim` knows the weapon each reload is drawn for, from the pack manifest), so no
  dark wedge is left where a forearm went behind the pistol or the barrel. The first drawing, a
  forearm sheared from the shoulder, was sent back by art review (2026-10-20): the off hand never
  showed side on, arms vanished and popped, the magazine was a few dark pixels in the foot; this
  replaced it, and three further review passes the same day tightened it (the jointed limbs; the
  magazine's drop, the seat's rise, outline wedges, the back view's stock and a soft rifle edge
  blending over the magazine; then the tube reload, the still back view, dips that never rise
  above the stance, the fresh magazine shown side on, and the weapon's drop home split over
  beats; then the pistol's magazine dropping out of the grip ahead of the shin and landing
  straight below on the next beat instead of sliding along the floor, a push for every shell,
  the west view's magazines and shells mirroring the east's pixel for pixel, a back edge kept to
  two pixels where the far arm passes under it, and a pixel or two off a wedge, a trigger guard, a
  muzzle and the floor magazines). The review strips are 48x56 cells with the body on the same
  baseline as every other strip; in game every reload frame is the 32x40 canvas on sole row 39. Per-frame `head`, `torso` and `hands` ride every new member, so A6's clothing and
  A9's weapon turn compose on them by the A7 contract. Five generations were spent (the three
  kept strips, the back view, and a four-views-in-one trial). **Not built:** drawn zombie walk
  in-betweens (the brief's added scope; still A7's one-pixel shifts), and a swing per weapon
  class -- both are in what's left as generation budgets.

  **Evidence:** `npm run godot:check:action` → `ACTION_OK`, chained after `godot:check:motion`.
  CATALOGUE: 10 families, 496 frames (1036 since the next record), every view present and equal (the crawl only east and
  west); an undeclared action, a crawl seen from the south and a face-on key carry none.
  TIMING and PRIORITY hold `action_index` and `action_key` (ends, wraps, holds, a one-shot over a
  stance, nothing upright while lying, nothing for nothing, the magazine reloads six to eight beats
  and the tube up to twelve, all held on the stance). REACH: all three reloads in every view move the weapon hand (two
  pixels, or one for a long gun from behind), bring the off hand to the weapon and away and end
  on the stance; the three-beat head-bob reload they replaced is refused. GEOMETRY: **428** (968 since)
  derived frames carry only their rest view's colours (a reload's magazine the held pistol's
  gunmetal, the tube reload's shells the shells icon's colours, and every one of the twelve
  reload views shows its own load and not the other's; the rest view shows neither), a crouch stands lower than the rest and a fall lower
  than the crouch, the crawl is wider than tall; a painted pixel is caught. STATES: the clock's
  named states are the sim's enum values. CLOCK: each event starts its one-shot on its own body,
  a repeated death does not restart a fall, a body never drawn does not fall, a wind-up strikes
  only into Recover. PUBLISHERS: all five event arms are published under `godot/sim/`. READERS:
  the three `main.gd` hooks, each shown missed when removed. SCENE, the dead-socket half, on the
  booted scene with real steps and the real draw: weapon.fired drew `body_survivor_recoil_e_0`;
  the swing command `..._swing_e_0` through the wind-up and `..._swing_e_1` on the strike; the
  Reload state `..._reload_e_0` with the player's own weapon, `..._reload_long_e_0` with a
  rifle put in hand and `..._reload_tube_e_0` with a pump shotgun; the crouch and crawl stances `..._crouch_e_0` and
  `..._prone_e_0` with no worn layer; one attack.connected drew the zombie's lunge and the
  player's flinch; entity.staggered the zombie's stagger; a killing head blow its fall in the
  corpse pass and then the settled body -- each against the same body without it. With the
  `_process` and `_draw_entities` hooks cut, every SCENE lane goes red. `godot:check:authored`
  and `godot:check:worn` hold the new members to the pack's geometry (action frames are allowed
  to stand lower and to move a layer point up to 10 px); `sprites:check` reproduces every one.
  Before/after strips and GIFs per action, for the eight bodies there were before the screamer
  and the bloater joined, are under
  `.hermes/plans/2026-10-19_a8-actions/`.

- **Feel — falls that lie down, and lunges that reach, 2026-10-20.** Art review's first pass over
  the screamer and bloater strips (NOT CLEAR: three blocking, eight major) found the fall broken
  for every family, the survivor's included. A fall was two frames of the body sinking straight
  down into its feet, then a cut to the corpse picture drawn centred on the ground point: the
  body jumped eight to eleven rows up and sideways on the cut, the bloater's boots vanished for a
  frame, and every view landed with its head east, so a body falling west turned round as it hit.
  The lunge snapped back two or three pixels on its last beat, skated its feet, held a frame
  twice on the bloater's east view, and from the north and south was a stretch or a duck. The
  second pass (NOT CLEAR again) measured the first fix: a three-frame turn to 60 degrees and a
  cut to the pack's corpse still changed the body's mass by up to a third in one beat, a landing
  beat two rows up read as a hop, and the north lunge lost a fifth of its body on one step. It
  set the bounds the fall now keeps on every beat: mass at most 15%, the centre of mass at most
  4 columns, no edge more than 6 px, and the lowest row never above the standing sole row. The
  third pass (NOT CLEAR, one major) found the lying frame was the knee buckle turned 90 degrees
  as a rigid block, and ruled that the pack's corpses are the quality floor: the fall ends on
  them. It also accepted the fall's rate, gave the stagger's first push a row, and named three
  minors (below). The fourth (NOT CLEAR, one blocking) confirmed the corpse, the mirrored runner,
  the belt and the stagger, and found the side views' settle dissolving the head away first and
  drawing the corpse's in last, so the body lay headless for a beat or three and the head popped
  back on the hold frame; its ruling, the head carried whole and a gate that sees it, is below.

  **The fall ends on the pack's corpse.** The knees go (a fold over the feet, which are kept to
  the end; the hip's top rows are drawn again over the sunk body, so a belt or a suit's taped
  waist stays painted), then the body is turned 10 degrees a beat, 10 to 80, about the outer edge
  of its leading sole toward the side it falls to (`motion/actions.py` `turn_about_feet`):
  RotSprite's way, up eight times by Scale2x, turned by sampling in whole-number sines and cosines
  (`TURN_TABLE`), and back down, so every pixel is one of the pack's. Only the edge the turn
  opened is ringed again, in the bare body's darkest colour (`_reoutline`); the pack's own edge
  keeps its own colours. A side view falls the way it faces; the front view crumples east and the
  back view west (`FALL_SIDE`, in `actions.py` and `presentation/appearance.gd` alike). Then it
  **settles** (`settle_plan`, `settle_frames`) onto the family's own pack corpse, prone for a
  side view and supine for the front and back (`LIE_POSE`), mirrored to the side it fell to, so
  the east and west views, and the south and north, land as exact mirrors of each other (the
  runner's included). The heavy's and the bloater's corpses, slimmer than the bodies that walked,
  are widened by whole sixteenths until they carry at least 95% of the last turned frame's mass
  (`lying_corpses`, `BELLY_PCT`); the armored's prone corpse, lighter than its armour-bulked
  body, is widened by the same rule, a sixteenth. The beats between are the turned frame
  becoming the corpse by count, the corpse's pixels nearest the body arriving first and the
  turned frame's farthest leaving first, the sole row last to go, each beat keeping only its
  largest connected run so no speck floats. **A side view carries its head whole**
  (`HEAD_CARRIED`, art review round 4): it lands face down with its head at the top of the
  corpse, rows above where the turned frame's head lies, and a dissolve by distance dropped the
  one head first and drew the other last. So the turned frame's head (`fall_head`: the pixels the
  turn sampled from the standing head, `head_of`, its top rows down to the neck and back from the
  face as far as it is tall) moves as one block, k/n of the way to the corpse's head
  (`corpse_head`) on beat k, drawn over the body; the rest dissolves as before, the corpse's sole
  row first. The front and back views, landing on their backs with the head about where it
  fell, carry theirs the same way since the follow-up below, and on every view the head takes
  the corpse head's colours and shape over its last beat (`HEAD_FADE`): half on the last beat,
  the rest on the hold frame. That is a half swap, each pixel changing once, not a soft fade
  (round 6 accepted it as such). Lying on its back, the corpse's head is the end of the body,
  `HEAD_INSET` columns in from its end column at that column's middle row; the top of the
  fall-side third, which a face-down body's head is, is an arm or the chest there (round 6
  found 24 of 30 front and back settles carrying the head to the chest). The corpse is placed
  within ten columns of where it overlaps the last turn most, or of where its foot end meets
  the turned frame's, clear of the canvas edge; the front and back views lie in one place,
  mirrored, and the side views lie as a pair whose foot ends mirror within `SETTLE_MIRROR` (2
  columns), the pair whose feet move least from where each turned frame's lay (a drift within
  `SETTLE_FOOT`, 2 columns, counts as none), so a body settles where it fell rather than skating
  along the floor (round 4's stalker slid 9 columns, round 5's runner 6). The runner is the one
  exception to a 3-column drift: its two turned frames' foot ends lie 13 columns off mirror (its
  east and west turn frames are not mirror images of each other), so corpses that
  land where their mirror lands must move 11 columns between them. Mirror first, as shipped: it
  lands 6 columns each side, its corpses 1 column off mirror. Drift first, the alternative: its
  feet within 3 columns, its corpses 7 or more off mirror. Round 7's review judges whether the
  6 columns read as a skate; if so, drift first, since a slide shows in play and the side views'
  mirror does not. The fix that holds both: mirror the runner's west turn frames from its east
  ones. Every other side view lands within 3 columns and its
  corpses within 2 of mirrored (round 6 accepted 2 to 3). Each family takes the beat count whose side views
  drift least, then the fewest beats, that keeps every step inside the
  bounds with a margin (13% mass, 3.5 columns of centre, 5 px of edge, the sole row held), the
  last step judged on every corpse pixel that shows (alpha 16 and up, its soft edge included):
  three to five, so a fall is 13 to 15 frames (three for the armored, commuter, raincoat and
  screamer, four for the survivor, bloater, heavy and stalker, five for the runner and
  workwear). The frames lie out on a wider
  canvas, `fall_canvas`: 96 columns, the family's height, the standing body on its middle column,
  declared per member (`canvas` on the member, which `tools/sprites/build.py` and
  `Appearance.canvas_of` both honour). **The corpse is the fall's last frame, and the settled
  body**: `_draw_corpse` draws `Appearance.lying_key` (the fall's last frame for the view it fell
  from) where the fall stood, so the hold frame is the corpse and nothing cuts. The view a body
  fell from is remembered on the render clock (`anim_clock.gd` `landed_view`, 512 bodies), and a
  zombie's settled record carries the heading it died with (`visualRemains` gains an optional
  `facing`, kept only when it is a finite number; no save version bump, an older record lies as
  drawn), so it lies the same way after a load. The survivor's and the common zombies' falls play
  at 12 frames a second (83 ms a beat), the heavy's and the bloater's at 10 (100 ms); round 3
  accepted those rates over ten beats, and the settle keeps them per beat, so a fall now runs
  1.1 to 1.4 s.

  **The lunge** is five beats with the feet planted (a lean above the hip, never a step): a
  wind-back, the reach, the full reach, and two beats home, a pixel a beat, so the last frame
  is a pixel from the rest. From the front and back the upper body travels two rows a beat
  down-screen or up-screen without losing a row, and the feet stay where they stood (round 2's
  arms widening at full reach stepped the feet a pixel outward; it is gone). The stagger seen
  from the south lifts the body a pixel on its first two beats, from the north dips it. The
  bloater plays on the heavy's timing, 8, 6 and 10 frames a second, since at the common zombie's
  rates it read lighter than the heavy on the same canvas. The stagger's first beat seen from the
  south lowers the lowest row from 55 to 54: round 3 ruled it the agreed knock-back push, and the
  gate allows a stagger that one row and nothing else.

  **Evidence:** `npm run godot:check:action` → `ACTION_OK`. Its LANDING lane places every fall the
  way `_draw_corpse` does, rest view to the corpse: `LANDING OK 40 falls, 592 steps ... at most
  12.2% mass, 3.4 columns of centre and 5 px of edge a step (bounds 15%, 4, 6), the sole row held,
  each lying to its fall side as its own last frame`. Its negatives: the pack's corpse cut in
  straight after the turn breaks the bounds 88 times, the same falls at every third frame 40
  times, and a view or key with no fall answers no lying frame. HEAD looks for a head on every
  beat of all 40 settles, the last turned frame's or the corpse's (the fall-side end of each,
  `HEAD_COLS` 8 columns, and lying on its back the `HEAD_CORE` 64 pixels of it nearest the
  head's middle, matched colour for colour wherever it moved between the two), or the two
  together as much of the larger as a head handing its colours over shows, summed only where
  their boxes meet (round 6 found the sum counting a head on the chest and the corpse's own as
  one); and the carried head must end within `HEAD_LAND` (4 px) of the corpse's own head,
  located in the lying body: `HEAD OK 40 settles in every view, 152 beats: a head carried on
  every one, at least 51% of it ... the corpse's head adds at most 10.6% of the body at the hold
  frame (bound 15%); the carried head ends at most 3.4 px from the corpse's (bound 4)`, the
  least share the bloater's east view on its last beat. Its negatives: each settle with both
  heads erased where they were found is refused, all 40; two half heads apart are not one head,
  10 of 10; a head left where it fell is refused as a landing, 29 of 40. Round 4's art fails it
  in all 20 side settles, each with a beat under half a head, and round 6's in 10 front and back
  settles, ending its head 4.3 to 11.3 px from the corpse's. STRIKE (which replaced LUNGE_MASS) holds every lunge and stagger, rest to the
  beats and home, to the same 15% mass step and the sole row (`72 lunges and staggers ... at
  most 10.5%`, the commuter's north lunge; a stagger 1 row up on 18 steps, its allowance), and
  refuses a beat with its lower half cut off and a beat lifted past its allowance in all 72.
  GEOMETRY lets a fall carry its corpse's colours and holds the fall's last frame wider than
  tall. READERS needs `_draw_corpse` to call
  `lying_key` and `dressed_texture` and to record what it laid down, each shown missed when
  removed; the FALL scene lane kills a zombie on the booted scene and finds it lying as
  `body_zombie_commuter_fall_w_12` after the fall played. CATALOGUE counts 1040 frames, GEOMETRY
  972 derived frames on their rest view's colours.
  `godot:check:authored` judges a fall member at its own canvas (PACK cuts it whole,
  ZOMBIE_POSES holds it to its family's canvas and anchor, with a sound fall frame accepted and
  a wide picture that is not a fall, or a fall wider than the fall canvas, refused);
  `godot:check:worn` lets a fall frame move a layer point up to 40 px, a body's height, since at
  90 degrees the head lies where the hip stood; the REMAINS lane in `godot:check:zombie_art`
  round-trips the dying heading through save text and refuses a heading that is not a finite
  number.

  **The survivor falls, and lies, in its clothes** (with #171 and #174 merged in). The painter
  follows the fall: `clothing/action_wear.py` dresses the fall's source and turns it by the same
  `derive` call, ringed in the bare body's ink so cloth and skin share one outline, lays each
  action out on the garment's action sheet at its frames' own width (3072x160, a fall frame 96
  wide), and declares each fall member's `canvas`; a garment pixel the turn's ring lands on is
  made opaque, as cloth always is. The corpse it settles onto was never a standing frame, so
  `clothing/corpse_wear.py` labels the pack's lying human by its own colours (ink, the grey
  trousers, the tan tee, skin, hair and shoes, the face, the arms and hands) and paints each
  garment over the parts its shape covers, at the light of the corpse's own pixel, with the belt
  or a suit's taped waist and ankles where its trousers meet its tee and shoes; the beats are
  made from the dressed turn and the dressed corpse by the bare fall's own call. A survivor with
  no garment in a slot would lie in the pack corpse's own tee or trousers there (none is drawn so;
  what's left says why). 256 action frames, 296 members a garment (`godot:check:authored` WEAR:
  8584 painted frames). The clock records the outfit a body was
  last drawn in (`AnimClock.act`'s `outfit`) and `_draw_corpse` composes the fall and the lying
  frame through `Appearance.dressed_texture`. `godot:check:action` CLOCK proves the outfit rides
  the fall and a bare body falls bare, and that every fall frame composes dressed at its own
  canvas. `godot:check:worn` CANVAS holds each garment member to its rig frame's own canvas.
  Strips and animations, laid out as the game draws them, are in
  `/mnt/project-files/a8-actions/zombies/round7/` and, clothed,
  `/mnt/project-files/a8-actions/clothed/falls-round7/`. **Not done:** the south lunge's legs read
  about three rows shorter on its full reach than the rest view's; an action frame keeps only the
  pack's solid pixels (alpha 128 and up), so the faint soft-alpha specks at a standing body's edge
  are not on the action frames; the lunge's homeward beat repeats an outward one; the pack's
  corpses keep their hole, missing outline and own palette; and a bare survivor would lie in the
  pack corpse's tee, though none is reachable. All are in what's left.

  **The settle's follow-up** (art review rounds 4 and 5's minors, after #173). The head hands its
  colours over instead of swapping them on the hold frame: a pixel of the carried head landing on
  the corpse's head takes that pixel's colour, one landing off it goes and a corpse head pixel
  nothing lands on comes, half on the last beat and the rest on the hold frame, so the pixels the
  hold frame recolours in the corpse's head drop to about a third (the heavy's west view 11 of 37
  where it was 30 of 30, the bloater's south 28 of 91 where it was 43 of 93). An outline either
  picture draws that a beat buries inside the body takes the other picture's colour there, or
  its neighbours' (`settle_frames`): buried near-black outline pixels across every bridge fall
  from 3163 to 74, at most 4 in a beat, and the heavy's north view peaks at 47 dark interior
  pixels on its way to the corpse's 49, where it was 82. A garment's seam across the body is
