  handed over (`settle_frames`' `lines`, from `clothing/action_wear.py`): the corpse's belt or taped
  waist arrives first and the frame's goes evenly, so the hazmat suit's belt through the south
  settle runs 14, 12, 9, 7, 5 where it was 12, 4, 2, 3. The side views' paired placement closes
  the runner's slide as far as its mirror allows. Round 7 (art review round 6): the front and
  back views carry the head onto the corpse's head, at most 3.4 px from it by HEAD's measure
  where the reviewer found round 6's 6.9 to 10 px off on the chest, and their corpses lie in round 5's columns again, so round
  6's hold-frame shifts of 1 to 2 columns are gone; buried outline pixels left across every
  bridge are 68, at most 5 in a beat. The armored's prone corpse is the pack's 29x25, 306 pixels drawn 17/16 its
  size by the belly rule, 31x27 and 355 pixels (motion/README.md). Measured with a throwaway
  driver against main's committed sprites, deleted afterwards; the gates are HEAD and LANDING
  above.

- **Feel — the weapon turned to the cursor, and the blow felt, 2026-10-19.** Item A9 of the
  2026-10-19 alpha plan, with the owner's answer to its Q3 the same day: the cursor is the aimer,
  the weapon points at it and the body follows, the way Project Zomboid plays it. Before this a
  moving body faced where it walked and ignored the cursor, the held weapon could point only
  along four axes, a white line and an arc stood over the player as the only readout of aim, and
  a blow that landed changed nothing on the body it hit but the blood.

  **The sim: aim is a second heading, priced at a walk** (the what's-left piece of that name,
  docs/30's decoupled paperdoll decision 7). `sim/aim.gd` (`SimAim`) is the one copy of the rule.
  A body carries `facing`, where its feet go, and once the player has proposed one an `aim`. The
  `aim` command turns a standing body's feet and aim together, as the single heading always did;
  a moving one keeps its heading and turns only its aim, and only on Walk or a slower rung --
  `_integrate_movement` snaps a held aim back to the heading every tick at Jog and Sprint, and a
  rider's aim is the machine's. The shot (`ranged.gd`), the swing (`melee.gd`) and the eyes
  (`visibility.gd`) read `SimAim.radians_of`; an NPC turn (`npc_combat._face_at`) and a vehicle's
  pin turn the aim with the body, so a stale proposal never points a swing. The price is
  `SimRanged.cone_cap`: a moving shooter aiming away from where it walks has its cone widened
  **past** `WIDE_HALF` by `TWIST_WIDEN` (0.35) at a full about-face, in proportion to the turn, and
  a round may widen to that ceiling but never past it. **An absent `aim` reads as `facing`, and
  nothing but the `aim` command writes one, which only presentation pushes** -- so every fixture,
  every headless campaign and the balance harness describe exactly the world they did, and the
  FAST tier needed no driver and no re-baseline (it passed unchanged inside `godot:m2`).
  **No `SAVE_VERSION` bump**, against the piece's own note and by `kernel/serialize.gd`'s rule
  (a bump is for a save an older build would misread): a save without `aim` restores every body
  facing where it aims, which is what it was; the `visualRemains` precedent is the same shape.

  **The picture.** Your body shows the view its aim falls in and the held weapon is placed for that
  view exactly as before -- grip on the hand, barrel the view's way, mirrored only facing west --
  then turned about the hand pixel's centre by what is left of the aim (`Appearance.held_turn`,
  never more than an eighth of a turn), drawn as one textured polygon (`Appearance.held_quad`,
  `main.gd`'s `_draw_layer`); no transform, so `check_topdown`'s counters still read zero. The
  aim glides between ticks like the heading (`interp.gd`'s `aim`), and your own weapon draws the
  cursor's bearing the frame it moves whenever `SimAim.holds` says the next tick will take it.
  `input_map.gd` re-aims every frame once a real pointer has moved, because walking past a still
  cursor swings the bearing too; a run nobody has pointed at proposes nothing. The facing line
  over every body and the aim cone over the player are gone: the sway is a **reticle at the
  cursor** (`_draw_reticle`) -- four ticks and a faint ring standing off it by the cone's half-angle
  at the cursor's distance, dimmed while the weapon is not raised, firearms only, never a number.

  **The blow felt** (`fx_look.gd`, presentation only). A seen blow flashes the struck body white
  for 0.12 s (a silhouette of the body and what it wears, in the palette's new `hitFlash`, made
  once per picture) and jolts its picture 3 art px straight away from the striker, easing back
  over 0.18 s; the sim's position, the shadow and the world hash never move. A shot kicks the
  weapon 2 art px back along its turned barrel over 0.12 s: the recoil *frames* are A8's, and
  `FxLook.kick(entity)` is the hook they can key to. Neither varies with the blow -- a graze and a
  killing blow flash and jolt alike, and `_felt` reads no damage, part or weapon. A muzzle flash
  now leaves the turned muzzle (the sheet placed for the aim's view and turned about the same
  hand), from the hand of the frame the shooter was last drawn on (`note_frame`). `main.gd`
  changes: `_draw`, `_draw_entities`, `_blit_body`, `_layer_rect`, `_draw_effects`, and the new
  `_draw_layer`, `_blit_flash`, `_white_of`, `_draw_reticle`.

  **The body faces the cursor whichever way it walks.** The view is the aim's, never the walk's,
  so a walker aiming over their shoulder would otherwise run the facing view's walk forwards while
  carried backwards -- a moonwalk. The animation clock now steps such a body's cycle the other way
  (`AnimClock.backpedals`, handed the view's own direction by `_draw_entities`): ground covered on
  the far side of the view runs the same stride in reverse, a strafe square to the view steps
  forwards, and a body with no view to compare (every face-on rig) never backpedals. **The weapon
  you are wielding comes round in front.** A service pistol equips to the secondary hand, which
  `HELD_BEHIND` hides behind the body seen from either side, so the gun you fired was the hidden
  one. `Appearance.wielded_items` reads the item each live `rangedWeapon` and `meleeWeapon`
  profile was built from (items.gd's `source`), and a wielded weapon draws over the body seen from
  east or west (`WIELDED_OVER`) whichever hand holds it; seen from behind it stays beyond the body,
  and a weapon carried but not wielded keeps its hand's side.

  **Half shipped, and which half:** the legs still have the body's four views, so a backpedal is
  the view's walk reversed rather than a stride of its own (legs on the movement vector is still
  the decoupled paperdoll arc's); and the jolt is the picture only, by design, so a heavy blow does
  not stagger a body in the sim.

  **Evidence:** `godot:m2:aim` HEADING: a body never aimed reads its facing and grows no aim;
  standing still turns feet and aim; walking east aimed north keeps the feet east, sees north
  better than south, and widens the cone **0.550 → 0.725** (past `WIDE_HALF`); standing twisted is
  free; jogging refuses a proposal and snaps a held aim back; an NPC turn turns the aim; the shot,
  the swing and the eyes read it (a commented read refused). `godot:check:worn` AIM: **1,440**
  aims over 10 held weapons in both hands keep the grip on the hand and the barrel on the aim
  within 0.001 px, unkicked and kicked, at most 0.772 rad left after the view, and unturned the
  quad is exactly HELD's rect on all four views; an unturned quad off the axis, a backwards turn, a
  wrong pivot, and a draw loop ignoring the aim, the turn or the aim's view are each refused; HELD's
  draw-loop needles follow the draw into `_draw_layer` and `held_quad`. `godot:check:fx` FELT: a
  seen blow flashes 1.0 and jolts 3 px away from the striker, both fading to nothing; a graze and a
  killing blow are felt alike while a blow from the far side jolts the other way; a sourceless
  bite flashes without a jolt; nothing unseen starts anything; a real shot kicks and settles; the
  draw loop reads all three. TURNED: a real pistol shot aimed 0.5, -0.6 and 2.0 puts the flash's
  anchor on the turned muzzle and an axis shot keeps the plain rect; a walking frame's hand is
  used. DRAWN now also blits the flashes as polygons and proves the hit flash reaches the draw.
  `godot:check:topdown` and `godot:check:weather` follow the retired line and cone to the aim and
  the reticle; `godot:check:zombie_art`'s READERS order follows the facing line to `SimAim.radians_of`.
  `godot:check:topdown` TURN: a fifth of a second at pace through the real clock, walking away from
  an east view runs exactly the forward stride in reverse, and a strafe south and a body handed no
  front step forwards; `_draw_entities` hands the clock the view's front. `godot:check:worn` ORDER:
  the kitted actor wielding its far hand's pistol draws it over the body from e and w and under from
  n, and wielding the shotgun leaves the pistol behind (each fix sabotaged once and its lane went
  red). Before/after GIFs (aiming in a circle, aiming while walking, a hit, a backpedal, the
  sidearm seen from the side) are under `.hermes/plans/2026-10-19_a9-aim/`.

- **Gate infrastructure — the `godot:m2` chain runs as four CI shards, 2026-10-19.** The
  85-gate chain took 40m45s on one runner (job 118220307956, measured on 2b48fef), against the
  45-minute `godot-m2` limit. `scripts/m2-shards.mjs` splits it into four `godot-m2-shard` jobs,
  balanced by those per-gate times; `godot:m2:balance` alone (791 s) is the floor on wall time.
  `godot-m2` is now the aggregate required check and fails unless every shard passed. The gates
  that write the per-machine `user://` store share shard 3. `npm run check:shards` (`SHARDS_OK`;
  its self-test refuses five broken layouts) proves each chained gate is in exactly one shard.
  Unsharded `npm run godot:m2` is unchanged. Wall time of the sharded run: see the PR.

- **UI — first-day hints, 2026-10-19 (alpha A21, from the alpha plan, not an M2 piece).** The
  first time a container is in reach, a wound is open, a zombie has been seen or night falls, the
  HUD speaks one digit-free sentence in a "tip" card above the action bar. `presentation/onboarding.gd`
  picks the due hint from the sim's read models (`SimContainers.hud_clause`, the injuries component,
  `SimSightings.remembered`, the clock) and marks it seen when offered; the seen set rides the save
  beside the snapshot and comes back on load. A click on the card clears it and stops there; the
  hint is offered only while the street is playing. **Gated** by `godot:check:hud`'s ONBOARD and
  HINT-CARD lanes and `godot:check:play`'s HINT lane (a real click through the engine's dispatch, and
  the seen mark round-tripped through F5 and F9).
- **Performance — the world, baked, 2026-10-19.** Item A4 of the 2026-10-19 alpha plan. The
  ground, the walls and the roofs were drawn tile by tile every frame, and the loop asked
  `has_tile` of every tile to decide whether to draw it; at 1280×720 that loop alone was about
  half of the draw. Now every look a tile can take is drawn once per 8×8-tile chunk into
  RenderingServer canvas items that keep their commands (`presentation/world_layers.gd`), in five
  layers behind `main`'s own item: the tile as seen (LIVE), the room boards under a standing wall
  module (A2), the tile as the remembered map draws it (REMEMBERED), the roof sheet (ROOF) and the
  same sheet dimmed (ROOF_DIM). Which look shows on a tile is a per-frame question answered by
  `presentation/world_mask.gdshader` from two small textures — the shadowcast's own cells, and one
  byte a tile for EXPLORED (unpacked from the sim's bitset where it changed), ROOF and A2 —
  uploaded only when they change. Walking re-uploads a few kilobytes and rebakes nothing. A chunk
  rebakes when what it was drawn from moves: the zoom, the map object, the content tree or the
  seed drop every chunk; a map generation change re-signs each cached chunk (its tiles, ground,
  indoors flags, overlays and parked vehicles, with a one-tile apron) and drops the ones whose
  inputs changed, so a door or a board rebakes one chunk; snow is quantised to 64 steps and
  stale chunks rebake inside a 2 ms frame budget, at least one a frame. A layer with no tile to
  show in a chunk is hidden outright, which spares the renderer the shader over it. The helpers
  draw through `_pen` (main itself, or `presentation/canvas_pen.gd` during a bake) and
  `_bake_layer` swaps in a camera at the world origin, so every helper is unchanged but for that
  prefix. `Appearance._content_entry` now hits an id index per content tree instead of scanning
  the whole tree per lookup, which took the props from 0.23 ms per look to almost nothing.
  `_draw_entities` and everything drawn after the world are untouched; lighting (A10) composites
  over the layers and can read the same mask textures (`mask_textures()`) without rebaking.
  Screenshots against the parent commit differ by at most 5 of 255 levels per channel at zoom 64,
  32 and 16, standing and after a walk, roofs and remembered tiles included.
  **Half shipped, and which half:** `npm run godot:bench:frame`'s shipped-draw now meets the
  10 ms mean (**28.5 → 8.7 ms**, p95 38.4 → 12.0, same container, llvmpipe), but crowded-draw
  does not (**318 → 108 ms**): that is the thousand bodies, which is body drawing and A7's. Of
  what remains in shipped-draw about 2 ms is collecting entities, 2 ms the body loop (about 1 ms
  of it `HudRead.pawn_tag`), and under 2 ms nature, furnishings and props, still drawn per frame.

  **Evidence:** `npm run godot:check:world_bake` → `WORLD_BAKE_OK`, chained after
  `godot:check:motion`. MASK-RULE: the shader's bit constants and discard rule are
  `world_layers.gd`'s, read by a scanner first shown a copy with LIVE sabotaged to 2; each layer's
  rule matches the layer table written out in the gate, and no tile state shows two ground looks
  (a rule table with LIVE's deny dropped is shown to fail). SOCKET: `_draw` reaches the bake
  through `_draw_world` and never calls `_draw_district`, which `_bake_layer` alone reaches; the
  fifteen baked helpers draw only through `_pen`, the scanner proven on a fabricated bare
  `draw_rect(`. SNOW, on a bare `WorldLayers` with a slow fake bake: a full snow step rebakes 1 of
  12 chunks the first frame and every chunk carries it 13 frames later. BAKED, on the real scene
  at 1280×720: all 12 chunks under the view bake on the first frame, the ring finishes in 18, and
  unchanged frames and a one-tile camera step bake none. NO-LEAK, at boot, at a front door and
  five tiles back into the street (**407 / 302 / 426** seen, **0 / 0 / 15** remembered,
  **61 / 166 / 27** dark tiles): the mask's LIVE bit is the observer's `has_tile` and its EXPLORED
  bit the remembered map's on every tile in view, a dark tile shows no ground look and a seen one
  exactly one. CULL, same three places: no chunk hides a layer one of its tiles shows, and
  48 / 38 / 34 of 60 chunk layers are hidden. ROOF: the ROOF bit is on exactly the 64 tiles
  `RoofLook.roof_tiles` chose at the door. REBAKE: a ground change rebakes its own chunk and leaves
  a chunk two away alone, a bare `invalidateMap` rebakes none, a zoom step rebakes every chunk
  in view and a content tree swapped for a copy rebakes too. Sabotaged, the gate goes red: LIVE
  forced on everywhere fails NO-LEAK, a signature that ignores the map fails REBAKE, a cull that
  never shows REMEMBERED fails CULL. The look gates that read the old loop were re-pointed at the
  new path, never relaxed: `check_water` (the fill goes to `_pen`, with a negative for a fill to
  main's own frame), `check_light_look`, `check_trees`, `check_topdown` (order read in
  `_draw_world`), `check_roof_look` (the floor probe records per bake layer and reads the screen
  through `state_at`; the socket lane follows `_bake_layer`) and `check_memory_look` (the remembered
  rule read through `WorldLayers.shows`). docs/22 has the timings.

- **Colonist orders: go there, hold there, haul that — plan A16, 2026-10-20.** A colonist picked on
  the street takes three orders from the right-click menu. `go` walks to a tile and ends there.
  `hold` walks there and stands, taking no work, until it is stood down: the draft in effect.
  `haul` carries one loose item to the stockpile by the ordinary Haul job, and the item is reserved
  to that colonist from the moment the order lands. Needs and sulking still come first, and an
  unarmed colonist re-arms before taking an order. The HUD names what the colonist is doing, and a
  ring marks the destination on the map. Gate: `godot:m2:orders`, which checks that a walk arrives
  and ends; that a held colonist takes no work while a free colonist goes for the same item; that a
  haul stocks the item and refuses a stocked or packed one; that a stand-down is refused with no
  order; that an order drops the job in hand at once; that the words and the menu follow the sim;
  and that the record is plain values. Also `godot:check:context` and `godot:check:hud`. Not in this
  slice: a draft toggle apart from `hold`, a message when a destination has no route (the order ends
  quietly), and a colonist who is already hauling an item on their own when the order lands (the
  order ends when that colonist carries it off). Sim tick, `godot:bench:runtime`: mean 7.1 ms on the base
  commit and 7.2 ms with the slice (medians of three to six runs each, the same container; the
  spread between runs is about 1 ms), p95 about 10 ms both ways, inside the alpha target of a mean
  at or under 10 ms. Before and after shots: `/mnt/project-files/planning/orders/`.

- **Stockpile zones: the stockpile as tiles, slice S1 of the 2026-10-24 plan.** The stockpile is a
  zone the sim keeps (`godot/sim/modules/stockpile.gd`), a `stockpile` record on the player keyed by
  `"tx,ty"`. Until the first mark there is no record and the zone is the annex's indoor floor, so an
  unchanged colony and every save from before this slice read as they did. `stockpile.mark
  {x0, y0, x1, y1, on}` marks or clears a rectangle through the input phase. A tile can be marked only
  if it is open floor, dry, not a door, and explored by the player, indoors or out. A zone holds at
  most 400 tiles and an `on` rectangle covers at most 400; both refuse whole. A marked tile walled
  over leaves the zone and returns when opened. `SimNeeds.is_stockpile_tile` asks the zone, the Haul
  drop (`_stock_drop`) walks its tiles row-major, and the orders' haul test follows it. Beds stay on
  the annex floor (`SimNeeds.is_annex_floor`). Gate: `godot:m2:stockpile` (`M2_STOCKPILE_OK`): DEFAULT,
  MARK (a 3x3 in and out; a wall, a door and an unexplored tile refused; the cap; `stockpile.changed`
  heard twice), WALLED, READERS, SAVE (a marked zone round-trips, and a save with no record reads the
  default). Sabotage: an unexplored-tile check turned to `true` turns MARK red. Not proven yet: a ford
  (no explored ford on the seed's map, skipped out loud). The two gaps S1 named, a full Haul walk onto
  a marked outdoor pile and the raider looter reading the annex, are closed by S3 below. Sim tick,
  `godot:bench:runtime`, three interleaved pairs on this box: head mean 13.42, 13.25, 13.26 ms; base
  14.06, 12.88, 12.96 ms (medians 13.26 against 12.96, inside the box's roughly 1 ms spread). Both sit
  above the 8 ms target here, as main does on this box.
- **Stockpile hauling: items spread over the pile, slice S3 of the 2026-10-24 plan.** A hauled item
  or a cooked meal goes down on the emptiest free tile of the nearest patch of the stockpile zone
  (`SimStockpile.patches` and `drop_tile` in `godot/sim/modules/stockpile.gd`; `_stock_drop`,
  `_haul_drop` and `_lying_tiles` in `godot/sim/modules/jobs.gd`). Six items dropped in turn land on six
  tiles, not one. A haul keeps its drop point on the job (`dropX`, `dropY`) and re-chooses only when the
  point stops being a free zone tile. A pile marked beside a camp is its own patch, so the camp's
  stash closes here. The raider looter (`raiders.gd`'s `_is_stores` and `_loot_goal`) reads the zone
  instead of `SimHome.rect`, so a marked outdoor pile is looted. Gate `godot:m2:stockpile` gains SPREAD
  (six items, six tiles; the first-free answer stacks them and goes red), PATCH (a pile clear of the
  annex is its own patch; from beside it the drop is on the pile, from home at home), WALK (a Haul
  picks an item up beside an outdoor pile and stocks it on the pile), COOK (a meal lands nearest the
  fire, not the cook's feet) and RAIDER (a looter beside a marked pile heads for it, an item off the
  zone is not stores). Carried: the day half of the colony's walks moves, and that surfaced
  `godot:m2:jobs`'s guard lane on the one-tile doorway case in the "Two walkers hold each other" entry
  above. Main's watch fix (#210, `SimJobs.GUARD_REACH`) cleared it on the merge; the lane was not loosened.
  Bench, `godot:bench:runtime`, three interleaved pairs against main 21211eac: shipped tick (`shipped-tick`) head mean 16.76, 18.66, 18.02 ms, median 18.02; main 17.22, 17.28,
  17.09 ms, median 17.22 (+0.8 ms on the median, inside a head spread of about 2 ms on this box).
  Colony tick (`colony-tick`, 200 loose items) head 20.92, 19.90, 19.51 ms, median 19.90; main 19.88,
  19.35, 20.33 ms, median 19.88 (level). Both branches are over the 8 ms mean target here, as main is.
  The +0.8 ms on the shipped median is inside the noise here but not yet explained; it is not
  attributed to the drop walk until a per-system timing says where it is.
- **Marking the stockpile on screen, slice S2 of the 2026-10-24 plan.** Z picks up a brush (a `mark`
  focus in `godot/presentation/input_map.gd`, the `stockpile` binding; Ctrl+Z stays the prone rung).
  Under it a left drag pushes one `stockpile.mark` on over the dragged rectangle, a right drag one
  off, a click one tile; walking, the stances, pause and the speed keys still work, nothing attacks
  and the right-click menu is off; Escape or Z puts it down. The drag previews what the sim says the
  release changes (`SimStockpile.preview`, which `mark` now applies exactly), amber to mark and rust
  to clear, and nothing when the sim would refuse it whole; a mark let go while paused draws as
  pending until a tick takes it. The zone is drawn on the ground (`godot/presentation/stockpile_look.gd`,
  `_draw_stockpile` in main.gd): a cool steel wash and a dashed masking-tape rim, only on tiles the
  player has explored, dimmed through `Palette.remembered` out of sight, never over a roof, quieter
  at rest than under the brush, under the props and bodies. The HUD speaks the brush in words
  (`HudRead.marking_line`) and the legend has a Z row. Gates: `godot:check:play` MARK (the keys, the
  three drags, the street drag that marks nothing, the paused pending draw and its end, the zone on
  explored tiles only, the bar), `godot:check:memory` STOCKPILE (explored only, remembered dimmed,
  roof wins, one rim with no inner seams and the concave notch, the batch, the kept shape and the
  state bytes, the rim at 3:1 or better on seven grounds, the frame reaching it), `godot:check:hud`
  ACTION (the brush's lines digit-free), `godot:m2:stockpile` PREVIEW (preview is what the mark
  does, the cap refuses whole, the zone's signature moves with a mark and holds otherwise),
  `godot:check:shots` (`stockpile_mark`, `stockpile_rest`, and `stockpile_night`, the zone's edge
  through the campfire's pool on the board floor, added after art QA round 2; twenty scenes).
  Sabotage, each shown red: no push on release (MARK), no explored check in `cells` (STOCKPILE),
  `cells` ignoring the kept geometry (STOCKPILE), no pending entry on release (MARK), a constant
  signature (PREVIEW).
  Frame cost, `xvfb-run -a npm run godot:bench:frame`, three interleaved pairs against the same
  build with `_draw_stockpile` returning at once: the first cut, painting every tile fresh each
  frame, was 17.77, 17.61, 18.04 ms shipped-draw against 9.04, 10.86, 10.26, a regression. The zone
  is now kept by `SimStockpile.signature`, its paint batched (row-run fills, one `draw_multiline` per
  colour, in tile-grid coordinates offset as drawn) and rebuilt only when a zone tile's state, the
  brush or the zoom moves: shipped-draw 10.76, 9.38, 10.71 against 9.94, 9.66, 10.72; night-draw
  9.63, 10.10, 10.12 against 9.43, 10.85, 10.44, inside the box's spread. The bench holds the sim,
  so it measures the kept path; a tick reads the zone's state (about 0.3 ms for the 320-tile default
  zone on this box) and a change of state rebuilds the batch (about 1.5 ms). Shots, before and after
  at both sizes, are in the project's shared folder under planning/stockpile/s2. After art QA round
  1: the cap is 1000 tiles (`SimStockpile.MAX_TILES`, from S1's 400, which left about 80 past the
  default zone); the zone query the Haul drop asks every carrying tick (`SimStockpile.tiles`) now
  parses each key once and sorts natively, 0.67 ms at 320 tiles and 2.1 ms at 1000 on this box
  against 2.1 to 3.4 ms at 320 before, held to the old answer by WALLED (sabotage: no sort, no solid
  test, each red); the wash leans to night alphas in the dark, held by STOCKPILE's NIGHT half (by
  firelight at least its noon contrast on every ground, which the day alphas fail); the drag's
  preview (about 5 ms for a full 1000-tile rectangle) is asked once per change of the rectangle and
  shared with the bar, and the pending marks once per change; the bar says "Z / Esc — put the brush
  down" as two caps. Not in this slice: S3's placement, stash and looter, and S5's Colony-screen
  words.
- **The stockpile on the Colony screen, in words: slice S5 of the 2026-10-24 plan.** The Colony
  screen (J) says what the colony keeps, so a run can be planned without walking to the pile. A
  read model, `godot/sim/stockpile_read.gd` (`StockpileRead.summary`), gives one row per group in a
  fixed order (food, drink, medicine, ammunition, weapons, clothing and armour, tools and
  materials, other), each an amount word (none, one, a few for two to four, some for five to nine,
  plenty for ten or more, a stack counted as its count) and up to three item names, most numerous
  first. It reads what lies on the stockpile's tiles now (`SimNeeds.stockpile_items`), so it follows
  the zone S1 made; a group comes off fields the content already carries, so no content key was
  added. The block stands in the drawer's place, two columns of four, whenever nobody is picked,
  and a "the stockpile" button beside "their skills" shows it for a picked colonist, with "back to"
  their name where "their skills" was; the drawer is the same rectangle either way, so the grid
  never moves and the roster keeps every row it had (1280x720 measured: a ninth block under the
  drawer would cost the roster its rows). Names that do not fit a column whole are passed over, not
  cut, so a shorter one after them may stand. The panel reads the summary once a tick (about half a
  millisecond on a booted district) and afresh whenever the screen opens, so a drop while paused or a
  load onto the same tick is not shown stale. Gates: `godot:check:play` STOCKPILE (at both windows
  the words are the read model's and the names are its names in order; a pile emptied with no tick
  reads none, dim, naming nothing once the screen opens again; no digit but an item name `_name_is_allowed` allows, where an amount of "12" is
  refused; every row inside the drawer, which holds still between the pile and a person; the button
  shows the pile without moving the game's pick or queueing anything, a right click does nothing,
  a Focus chip's place queues nothing while the pile is shown, and the way back shows the person;
  both inks at 4.5:1 or better on the steel) and `godot:m2:stockpile` SUMMARY (an emptied pile
  reads none with a tin lying outside it; a stack of three tins and one of two read food "some",
  named most numerous first; a bandage reads medicine "one"; the amount ladder at each edge; every
  group has content that falls in it). Sabotage: the read model walking every loose item instead of
  the stockpile's turns SUMMARY and STOCKPILE red; a stack counted as one turns SUMMARY red; the
  button that does not flip turns STOCKPILE red; "none" drawn in the full ink turns STOCKPILE red.
  Review scenes `colony_stockpile` (nobody picked, a pile stocked across seven groups) and
  `colony_stockpile_picked` (the pile shown for Mara), both windows, with before and after of
  `colony`, `colony_picked` and `colony_crowd`. Not in this slice: taking from the Colony screen,
  and anything carried or lying outside the stockpile. No sim system changed, so no bench.
- **Taking from the stockpile: the loot window, slice S4 of the 2026-10-24 plan.** Standing in the
  stockpile, E opens the loot window on it, titled "the stockpile", beside the pockets. It lists every
  loose item on the patch the player stands in that the player sees from there, nearest first
  (`SimStockpile.in_sight`, `stores_view` in `godot/sim/modules/stockpile.gd`). The same drag,
  ctrl-click and "take all that fits" the cupboard window has send `stockpile.take` and
  `stockpile.put`, and the sim decides each one: a take is the ordinary pick-up without the 1.5 m
  reach, a put goes down by S3's drop rule on a tile of the patch in view. With the sheet open the
  stockpile is the sheet's first column, as a cupboard is. E's rung, the menu's row and the bar's
  words are in `godot/sim/modules/fortify.gd` and `godot/sim/context.gd`; the window is
  `godot/ui/inventory_panel.gd` (`_send`, `loot_capacity`) fed by `godot/presentation/main.gd`
  (`_stores_for_window`). Gates: `godot:m2:stockpile` TAKE (a tin in view taken and put back in view;
  a tin behind a wall on the same patch, a tin off the zone and a take with the window shut refused;
  off the zone the window shuts and a put is refused; E opens it on the pile and picks up off it),
  `godot:check:inventory` STOCKPILE (the window is the stockpile and lists the tins in view and not the
  walled or off-zone one; a ctrl-click takes, a drag puts back; a cupboard takes the window; a tile
  off the zone shuts it), `godot:check:context` BAR (a tin on the pile: E's words are the menu's first
  row), and the `stockpile_window` review scene in `godot:check:shots`. Sabotage: dropping the sight
  test lists the walled tin (TAKE red); removing the E rung picks the tin up (TAKE red); a put that
  pushes nothing leaves the tin in the pockets (STOCKPILE red). Frame cost, measured with a throwaway
  driver on the shipped district with 120 tins in sight: `stores_view` 3.8 ms, once per sim tick
  while the window is open (main.gd and the panel share one layout); the zone's patches are cached on
  the world, so finding the patch went from 7.1 ms to 0.01 ms. Nothing runs on the tick path but a
  close check over bodies with the window open, so no tick bench. Not built: a pile holding more than
  the window's cells shows the nearest and says "and more besides" rather than scrolling. At 1280x720
  the grid is eight by three so the window clears the action bar, and a pack (four cells tall) is
  reached from the sheet's column (Tab) or by "take all that fits". Shots, before and after at both
  sizes:
  `planning/stockpile/s4/` in the project files.
- **The stockpile drop point, brought down to cost (a follow-up to S3).** S3's drop
  (`_stock_drop` in `godot/sim/modules/jobs.gd`) ran once per haul pickup and once per cooked meal,
  and cost a single tick 6.6 to 7.3 ms on the 320-tile default zone and 20 to 28 ms at the
  1000-tile cap on this box. Most of it was String work: `SimStockpile.patches` keyed its flood
  fill and `drop_tile` its load count by `"x,y"`, and each patch sorted by a comparator. The free
  test also walked every bed and campfire for every zone tile. Now the patch walk and the load
  count key on the tile itself, a patch sorts by its row-major number, and `_stock_drop` reads the
  beds and fires once per drop into a set of taken tiles. The answer is unchanged. On seeds
  20260805 and 99, hashes of the patches, of forty drops in a row from sixteen points on three zones
  (default, default plus four far blocks, 1000 tiles), and of every ground item after 3000 ticks
  are identical before and after. Gate: `godot:m2:tick` DROP carries the String-keyed code and holds
  the shipped code to it: the patches, twenty-four drops in a row from eight points on two zones,
  and `_stock_drop` with a lit campfire on a zone tile. Its negative is a drop blind to the fire,
  which lands on the fire's tile, while `_stock_drop` must not. Sabotage, each shown red: no sort
  in a patch, no campfire in the taken set, a load that never counts. `godot:m2:stockpile` SPREAD
  and PATCH stay green. Cost, two interleaved runs a seed against main 3bb0bfd6, on this box: at
  320 tiles `patches` went from 2.9 to 3.1 ms down to 1.2 to 1.6 ms, and the drop from 6.6 to
  7.3 ms down to 1.7 to 2.0 ms. At 1000 tiles `patches` went from 9.8 to 10.9 ms down to 3.8 to
  6.4 ms, and the drop from 20.4 to 28.0 ms down to 5.0 to 8.0 ms. `tiles` is unchanged: 0.7 ms at
  320 and 2.1 to 2.5 ms at 1000.
- **The cook's raw: nearest the fire, never past the dead (the stockpile review, finding 7).**
  `_stock_cookable` (`godot/sim/modules/jobs.gd`) took the first raw food in entity order from
  anywhere on the zone, with no thought for distance or danger, and Cook was not in `DANGER_KINDS`,
  so a cook on that walk did not break off as a hauler would. Both were harmless while every raw
  lay on the annex floor; with a pile marked by a camp (slice S2), the first in entity order could
  be the far one, past the dead, and the cook walked to it. Now the raw nearest the fire wins
  within each pass (food first, then the rest, as before), a raw in danger is no candidate, and
  Cook is in `DANGER_KINDS`. Danger for a raw follows the rule the colonist's own body is judged
  by (`_outside_in_danger`): inside home's walls only a zombie inside the walls counts
  (`_zombie_inside_walls`), since the yard's dead stand within `DANGER_TARGET_METRES` of the annex
  floor on most seeds and a raw at home is as safe as home is; anywhere else it is Haul's rule for
  the ground it will walk to (`_cookable_in_danger`). Gate: `godot:m2:stockpile` FAR, with every
  zombie moved by hand and put back: a raw at home and one on a far pile beside a zombie, spawned
  first, and the home raw is cooked; only the far raw, and no Cook is offered; every zombie in a
  far corner, and the far raw is cooked; a second home raw spawned after the far one, and the
  nearest to the fire wins. Sabotage, each shown red: no danger skip (a Cook offered for the raw
  beside the zombie), first in entity order (the far raw taken over the home one). `godot:m2:jobs`
  COOK CLAIM and `godot:m2:transform` PINNED, COOK and ORDER went red under a danger test that
  counted the yard's dead against the annex floor, and hold green under the walls rule.
- **Three small things from the stockpile review (findings 8 to 10).** The cap counted tiles that
  were not stockpile: `SimStockpile.preview` judged `MAX_TILES` by the record's size, so a marked
  tile walled over since (out of the zone, `has_tile` false) still held a place against the cap.
  It now counts the record's live tiles (`_live_count`, `count` without the sort), as `count` and
  the Colony screen do. Two comments said what was no longer true: `jobs.gd`'s head note that
  `_stock_drop` does not follow home "because the stockpile is the annex's indoor floor" (it
  follows the nearest patch of the zone since S3), and `stockpile.gd`'s note that the Haul drop
  asks `tiles` every tick a hauler walks (it asks once per pickup since S3 and keeps the point on
  the job). And docs/33 now carries the feature's five cards and the one tuning call to object
  to, which the plan posted in the planning thread and nothing in the repository recorded. Gate:
  `godot:m2:stockpile` PREVIEW's cap case (a zone one short of the cap with a walled key takes
  one more tile and refuses two; the record counted by size refuses the one, shown red) and SAVE's
  new half (the open window and a claimed tin round-trip a save; a save with no `stockpileOpen`
  record loads shut). No sim behaviour changed but the cap's count.
- **Nowhere to put it: the two ways a hauled or cooked thing left the map (the stockpile review,
  findings 1 and 2).** The feature's end-to-end review (`planning/stockpile/review.md` in the
  project files) found two paths that lost an item for good. A Haul or Repair pickup whose stow
  failed (`_do_haul`, `_do_repair` in `godot/sim/modules/jobs.gd`) had already taken the item's
  `position` off and stopped, leaving it on no tile and in no pack; a probe with the zone emptied
  lost four of six tins in fifty ticks to Ellis's full stack. And with no stockpile tile anywhere --
  one right-drag over the annex empties the zone -- a cooked meal was spawned without a position,
  and every loose item near home became a haul that ended in the hauler's pack. Now a refused stow
  puts the `position` back and holds the colonist off Haul and Repair for `HANDS_FULL_TICKS` (600,
  the `handsFull: {tick}` record, absent by default so no save changes); a meal with no free zone
  tile lies at the fire's own tile; and while the zone has no tile (`SimStockpile.has_any_tile`,
  which stops at the first live tile) the Haul search offers no item and the haul order row is
  absent (`SimOrders._haulable`); the corpse dump is not the stockpile and is still offered. Gate:
  `godot:m2:stockpile` EMPTY (the zone emptied: no Haul offered or ordered over sixty ticks, the tin
  stays on the floor and in nobody's pack, the meal lies at the fire; one tile marked again makes
  the tin a haul) and FULL (a helmet a shut pack refuses lies where it lay, the hauler's hands read
  full, no Haul is offered during the hold and it comes back after; the positive, the helmet
  offered with hands free, is proven first). Sabotage, each shown red: the old `_do_haul` (the
  helmet at no tile), the old `_do_cook` (the meal at no tile), the old `_haul_work` (a haul with no
  zone). Whether emptying the zone should be allowed at all is on a card to the owner; this keeps it
  allowed and honest. No balance claim: the paths it closes never fired on the shipped default zone
  unless a pack was full.
- **The patches read once, and "take all" at cost (the stockpile review, findings 3 to 5).** The
  drop point (`SimStockpile.drop_tile`) walked the zone's patches afresh on every haul pickup, cooked
  meal and re-choice, 2.7 ms on the default zone and 3.0 at 960 tiles, while `_patch_index` kept the
  same answer for the window at 0.04 ms; `patches` is served from that index now (the walk is
  `_walk_patches`), and the index is keyed by the tile throughout, closing the entry above's open
  item (`_patch_index` and `put` keyed on `"x,y"` Strings; `patch_under` hands back a set keyed by
  `Vector2i`, and `context.gd`'s menu row reads it so). `get_meta` with a null default raised an
  engine error on every world's first ask (one line in four gate logs on main); `has_meta` is asked
  first. "Take all that fits" asked `in_sight` again for every take, a line-of-sight test per thing
  per take: 120 tins in sight cost 182 ms in one tick; the list is read once and handed to each
  take, and a footprint the pack has refused is not tried again for a thing that can neither merge
  nor be worn: 47 ms. Measured with the review's probe on the gate's boot: `patches` 2.66 to 0.30
  ms (320 tiles) and 2.97 to 0.33 (960), `_stock_drop` 2.91 to 0.26 and 3.02 to 0.30, `take_all`
  182 to 47 ms. Same answers: `godot:m2:tick` DROP still holds the patches and twenty-four drops to
  the String-keyed oracle; `godot:m2:stockpile` PATCH now also holds `patches` to the fresh walk
  after a mark joins a tile to the pile and after a wall splits it (sabotage: an index blind to the
  map generation, red), and TAKE gains "take all" taking exactly the tins in view. Nothing drawn
  changed. The engine error has no lane: a gate cannot read its own stderr, so the guard is the
  record.
- **E on the stockpile answers for the patch underfoot (a follow-up to S4).** S4's `e_opens`
  (`godot/sim/modules/stockpile.gd`) asked whether the nearest loose item lay on the *zone*, while
  the window it opens lists the *patch* the player stands in. With two patches an arm's reach apart
  and a tin on the other one, E opened a window that could not list the tin, and the bar's words
  promised "go through the stockpile" for a tin the window never showed. `e_opens` now asks
  `on_own_patch`, the patch the actor stands in, so a tin on a neighbouring patch is picked up as
  anywhere else and the same tin on the player's own patch is still the window. The menu follows
  E (the review's second half of the finding): `SimContext.verbs_at` builds the stockpile row once,
  puts it first when no cupboard is in reach, where it is what E does, and after the pick-up and
  the cupboard rows when a cupboard is in reach, where E keeps its old ladder; so the bar's E words
  and the menu's first row agree on the pile as they do everywhere else. Nothing on screen changed
  but the order of two rows in that one case. Gate: `godot:m2:stockpile` NEXTDOOR (a tin on the
  next patch inside the pick-up reach is picked up and the bar says "pick up"; moved onto the
  player's patch it makes E the window; both halves fail on the old `has_tile` test) and
  `godot:check:context` BAR's new case (a tin on the stockpile beside a crate: the bar's E words
  begin "pick up", the menu's first row is the same, and the stockpile row is still offered).
- **Attack order: a picked colonist goes after one zombie or raider they can see — 2026-10-24 orders slice A2.**
  With a colonist picked on the street, the menu's "have Mara attack it" row offers an `attack` order on a
  zombie or raider the colonist or the player can see right now (`SimOrders.accepts`, the scarce-information
  rule). The colonist walks to the target's tile, re-planning when it moves or every ten ticks, and stops
  where `SimNpcCombat.can_strike` says a blow or a shot lands. npc_combat's `_nearest_threat` picks the
  ordered target over a nearer one while it is inside the envelope. The order ends when the target is gone,
  when nobody has seen it for `SimSightings.FRESH_TICKS`, or when the colonist is critically injured (the
  break-off rule from npc_combat). Gate: `godot:m2:orders`'s ATTACK lanes (a walk reaches the target and
  lands a blow; the pick prefers the ordered target to a nearer one; the row and the order are refused for
  an unseen zombie, a colonist and a corpse; a critically injured colonist loses the order). Not built:
  the ordered target is picked, but the blow itself is melee.gd's: a swing lands on whatever is nearest
  inside its arc, so a nearer zombie in front can still be struck. Whether the arc should honour the
  order is not asserted. Night sight: a survivor sees 1.9 m at night (docs/23's night reach), so the lanes
  run at midday.
- **Draft key: X holds a colonist where they stand, X again sets them free — 2026-10-24 orders slice A1.**
  With a colonist picked on the street, X pushes the command `SimOrders.draft_command` decides: a
  `hold` on the tile they stand on, or a `clear` when they already hold an order. A drafted colonist
  takes no work and stays put; the menu's "hold here" and "go here" rows are unchanged. The player,
  a grabbed colonist, a corpse and a recruit are refused. JT picked the key (docs/30, "The draft key
  on X, 2026-10-24"). Gate: `godot:m2:orders`'s DRAFT lane (an undrafted control takes the work, the
  drafted colonist does not for 2,400 ticks and strays nowhere, the second press frees them and they
  take it, the refusals), and `godot:check:play`'s DRAFT lane and KEYS row (X with Mara picked pushes
  the hold, X again the clear, X with nobody picked pushes nothing).
- **Unreachable-spot callout: an order that cannot be done says so — 2026-10-24 orders slice A3.**
  An order ends with a reason, published as `order.ended` by `SimJobs.end_order`: `arrived` (a walk or a
  hold reached its spot), `stood-down` (the player cleared it), `gone` (the haul item or the attack target
  went), `broke-off` (the critical-injury rule), or `no-route` (a walk or a haul found no path). Only
  `no-route` is said aloud: speech.gd's `order.no_route` handler makes the colonist say a line from
  `speech.order.no_route` (two lines, digit-free). The other endings stay silent. The haul offer also
  refuses an item another live colonist's Haul job is carrying off (its `reserved` claim names that
  colonist and the job), so the menu never sends two colonists to one item; a reservation alone, with no
  job yet, does not withhold the item. Gate: `godot:m2:orders`'s ENDINGS lane (a walk into a walled-off
  pocket ends `no-route`, a reachable walk ends `arrived`) and COLLIDE lane (the free item is offered, the
  one another colonist carries is refused, and a reservation with no job does not refuse), and
  `godot:check:speech`'s NO-ROUTE lane (no-route is said from its entry, the other endings say nothing).
  A haul that finds no path ends `no-route` too, so it is said as well. Bench, `godot:bench:runtime`: see the PR.
- **UI — the sheet and Work grid fit the reviewed viewports, 2026-10-03.** At 1280×720,
  inventory now separates its equipment, native 56-pixel bag cells and inspect pane, keeping
  all seven frame-pack columns reachable. The compact sheet uses the condition chart at integer
  2×; the wide sheet retains 3×. Condition prose wraps and scrolls independently of bags.
  Closing inventory hides the clipped bag child, and bag pick/cursor/drop paths reject points
  outside the visible clip. Work columns share measured widths for drawing and input; the
  roster determines panel height, with scrolling for extra survivors. Work and the skill web
  hide the corner chart even while soft-paused. No simulation, art, typeface or information-policy
  change. The corner chart/action-bar overlap was already fixed by D2, not by this slice.

  **Evidence:** INVENTORY's new LAYOUT lane checks geometry, condition scrolling, closed-child
  visibility and clipped drop refusal. PLAY's WORK-LAYOUT lane resizes the real scene, clicks
  the last priority column, checks overflow-roster scrolling and the entity selected after
  scrolling, and checks paused corner-chart hiding/restoration. Inventory, play, UI skin, HUD
  and response focused checks pass; independent source and screenshot review found no blocker.
  [Forty native viewport captures](../.hermes/plans/2026-10-03_ui-layout/README.md) compare ten
  scenarios before/after at 1280×720 and 1920×1080, including healthy/injured inventory, pack
  scrolling, Work, HUD, title/pause/settings and an edge item menu. Below-minimum layouts,
  every possible long description and a human campaign remain outside this evidence.
  Combined verification is recorded with the October integration below.

- **UI asset delivery — the approved UI Field Kit, 2026-09-20.** The owner-approved
  kit is versioned under `godot/art/simplyzombies-ui/`: 120 native RGBA PNGs across
  76 logical assets, a 512×512 atlas, 24 StyleBoxTexture resources, a Theme, four
  animated SpriteFrames, pixel font and license, cursors and a CanvasItem helper.
  A native demo, offline preview, sources and rebuild tools accompany the resources.
  `python3 godot/art/simplyzombies-ui/tools/validate_assets.py` passes 998 checks;
  Godot 4.7.1 running `res://art/simplyzombies-ui/tools/validate.gd` passes 349 checks;
  `node godot/art/simplyzombies-ui/tools/verify_preview.cjs` passes 19 checks over
  four rendered views. Typecheck, lint and formatting pass. All 82 M2 gates pass
  across the initial lethality run, a fresh stats retry after a stalled process,
  and the remaining 80 scripts in chain order, with no gate or assertion changes.
  `docs/repository-delivery.json` inside the kit records that detail. A browser-window
  smoke test was not performed. This delivers assets and a demo; applying the skin
  to the live CanvasItem UI remains separate work. Preview sample counts do not
  amend the information or digit bans, and no open renderer slice or owner decision
  is closed by this delivery. That live-UI work is now named in [what's
  left](#whats-left-in-milestone-2)'s "UI — the UI Field Kit, live" group, decided
  by the owner 2026-09-25.

- **UI — the chrome wears the kit, 2026-09-25.** The first piece of the "UI Field Kit, live"
  group ([docs/30](30-decisions.md#the-ui-field-kit-live-2026-09-25)). A new `ui/kit.gd` is the
  one door to `godot/art/simplyzombies-ui/`: it loads the kit's PNGs the two-path way
  `appearance.gd`'s `resolve()` does (verified headless on this container: every kit `.tres` and
  `theme.tres` load null with "referenced non-existent resource", a kit PNG has no loader, and
  `Image.load` reads it), scales each 2× with nearest filtering once at load, and builds cached
  `StyleBoxTexture`s — keyed by id, centre and opacity to the whole percent — from a `NINE` table
  of the manifest's native margins, doubled when built, the centre tiled, and null for a rect
  smaller than those margins so the caller falls back to a drawn fill. `ui/chrome.gd` keeps every
  colour, `HEADER_H`, `FONT_SIZE`, `font()` and every caller's signature: `panel` is
  `panel_standard` drawn twice, the frame at its opacity and the border alone 0.15 above it;
  `header` keeps its strip, inset inside the frame's border, over the kit `divider`, with an
  optional small glyph before the label; `cell` is `slot_empty` (the pocket grid's 52 px cells
  clear the doubled 24 px of margin, and the bench's rows clear it too); `item_plate` is
  `panel_inset` (the smallest plate, 48 px, clears 40). The dead `pin()` and `BRACKET` are gone.
  **Gated** by `npm run godot:check:ui_skin` → `UI_SKIN_OK`, new, last in the `godot:m2` chain:
  KIT holds `NINE` to `manifest.json` and every `styles/*.tres` as text, holds every kit chrome
  id to worn-or-unused-with-a-reason, and names the three departures — `OWNER_SCALE` 2,
  `CENTRE_MODE_DEVIATION` (the centre tiles, not the `.tres` stretch), the keycap alone at 1× in
  `Kit.NATIVE_STYLES` — refusing eight fabricated disagreements, among them a tiled style with no
  deviation named and a deviation naming no departure; RESOLVE resolves all 18 worn textures and
  all 32 glyphs at both sizes headless at the manifest's size times their scale, and a made-up
  one to null; PANEL builds the style at a set opacity with doubled margins, cached, and refuses
  a rect one pixel under them, then follows `panel`, `cell`, `item_plate` and `header` one call
  deep to `Kit.style(` and `.draw(`, refusing a rect-only body, a dead link and a commented
  needle; HELPERS refuses a public chrome helper with no caller in `godot/ui/` or `main.gd`.
  FONT, GLYPHS, KEYCAPS, OUTLIERS, CURSORS, MOTION and EVENTS print `SKIP <LANE>: not landed`,
  one function each, for their slices to replace. The sabotage pass turned the gate red ten ways
  before this landed — a wrong margin in `NINE`, `Chrome.panel` with the kit only in a comment,
  an uncalled helper, `slot_empty.png` removed, a pending helper given a caller, a tab style
  worn, the deviation set to stretch, the deviation emptied, the code set back to stretch, and
  `SCALE` set to 1. **What is half-shipped, on purpose:** `frame`, `keycap` and `glyph` have no
  caller outside `chrome.gd` yet — HELPERS lists them as pending, prints a SKIP naming the slice
  that reads each, and goes red the moment one gains a caller without leaving that list; the
  font is still the engine fallback until "One typeface"; and some screens' content gutters,
  sized for the old hairline, now sit close to the ten-pixel border, which that same slice
  refits. **Edges by style, the owner's decision the same day**
  ([docs/30](30-decisions.md#the-ui-field-kit-live-2026-09-25)): a `StyleBoxTexture`'s axis modes
  cover its edge strips as well as its centre, so tiling both axes drew a fragment of every button
  and slot bracket along every border as a row of tick marks, while stretching the edges lengthens
  a dashed line's dashes and every bracket arm in them. `Kit.style` now hands back a cached
  `Kit.Style` pair drawn by one `.draw()`: the frame, drawing no centre, and the centre alone
  (`region_rect` the texture inside the frame's margins), always tiled. `slot_empty`, the six
  panels and the divider tile their edges (`Kit.EDGE_TILED`); the buttons, the other slots and the
  keycap stretch theirs (`Kit.EDGE_STRETCHED`). Where a corner piece runs past the manifest's
  margins the style draws at `Kit.WIDENED_MARGINS`, widened just enough to hold it: seven
  bracketed styles (the focus button's to [18, 10, 17, 10] native) and, by the owner's follow-up
  the same day, three panels whose corner highlight the tiled edge had repeated as a tick down the
  rim (the pause dialog's to [14, 13, 12, 12]), plus `panel_danger` at [10, 11, 10, 10] set by
  eye, because its red rim breaks along its whole length. KIT holds every consumed style to
  exactly one group and each frame to its group's mode and margins; re-measures every frame's
  corner piece on the native pixels (no ink carried across a margin into an edge strip, and a
  pixel less on any widened side lets some through), with `panel_danger`'s remaining runs — the
  rim's own — pinned at three and each of its widened sides required to remove one; and checks
  every surface a style draws on, the HUD cards and dialogs included, still clears its doubled
  margins. Twenty-six fabricated disagreements are refused, among them a style in both groups and
  in neither, a tiled-edge frame that stretches, a bracketed one that tiles, the focus button and
  the pause dialog each at the kit's own margins and a pixel wider than they need, and
  `panel_danger` at the kit's margins.

- **UI — one typeface, 2026-09-25.** The second piece of the "UI Field Kit, live" group
  ([docs/30](30-decisions.md#the-ui-field-kit-live-2026-09-25)). `Chrome.font()` loads the kit's
  `fonts/VT323-Pixel.res` lazily — never through `preload`; it is a self-contained FontFile and
  loads headless — and hands back one cached `FontVariation` over it, antialiasing and hinting
  off as the kit configured them, the engine's fallback font in its fallbacks, and the "fi"
  ligature off (VT323 carries one, which on a monospace pixel face drew "first" a cell short).
  Every screen draws with it: `hud.gd`, `legend.gd`, `work_panel.gd`, `paperdoll.gd`,
  `dashboard.gd` (three layouts) and `main.gd`'s pawn tag no longer name `ThemeDB.fallback_font`,
  and nothing under `godot/ui/` or `godot/presentation/` but `chrome.gd` does. **The size
  ladder is 20 / 25 / 30 / 50** (`Chrome.LADDER`): 25 and 50 are VT323's pixel-exact sizes (a
  0.04 em grid), 20 and 30 are one rung either side where a layout needs them. Every old size
  moved by one rule — VT323's capitals are 0.56 em against the engine font's 0.71, so an old
  size times about 1.3, snapped to the nearest rung, keeps the capital height and the line
  height near where they were while each line comes out a little narrower: 13–16 → 20, 18–20 →
  25, 22–26 → 30, the title's 52 → 50. So the HUD cards and the action bar's clauses, the
  bench's and inspect pane's titles, the shell's rows and the dashboard's motion word are 30;
  body text, the header labels, the legend and the quick strip's names are 25; the skill web's
  words, the work grid's column heads and clauses, bag names and every footer hint are 20; the
  title and the car's gear letters are 50. **Refit around the new metrics:** the legend is two
  wrapped columns filled in reading order and broken where the taller column is shortest (a
  group the break cuts in two repeats its name), its key cell a 150 px cap with a wider key on
  its own line, stepping down to 20 when it will not fit the window — it had been one 1320 px
  column 1342 px tall, spilling off a 1080 screen with the E row running off its right edge — and
  it is now added to the UI layer after the corner doll and the quick strip, whose layer used to
  draw over its wash; the "F1 to close" hint is measured, not a fixed 156 px back from the edge;
  `work_panel`'s header fits at 25 (it overran 1520 px at the engine font) and its focus word's
  reserve is the longest word's width; `bench_panel`'s condition word is measured and
  right-aligned rather than a fixed `col_w - 96` that cut "barely holding" off, its rows taller
  so a line clears the slot frame's dashes; the dashboard's lamps are one measured, centred row
  and each dial's word hangs under it in its own row above the rule (the car's panel 600 × 200,
  the handlebar's 460 × 160, the board's 320 × 80), where before the words sat on the rule and
  the fuel word ran past the panel; the action bar steps a rung down when the window is too
  narrow for it and is capped at the window's width, which a `clampf` with its floor above its
  ceiling had not done on a 1280 window. **The 2× frame's crowded gutters:** the HUD cards'
  gutter is 24 (was 14 against a ten-pixel border), the pockets header's "on you" sits 22 in on
  the header label's own line, the body panel's slots and hint line 24 in, the word menu's pad
  22 × 12. Header labels are centred in the strip from the face's metrics
  (`Chrome.header_baseline`), and a word's click rectangle is built from `Chrome.ascent` and
  `Chrome.line_height`: a Font's own metrics are the tallest of it and its fallbacks, so the
  variation reports the engine font's 35 px line at 25 where every glyph it draws is VT323's 25
  — the skill web's click targets overlapped on it until the rectangles used the face's.
  **Gated** by `godot:check:ui_skin`'s FONT lane, in five parts each red both ways: FACE holds
  `Chrome.font()` to a cached variation over the kit's VT323 with the engine font behind it and
  the ligature off, and refuses a variation over the engine font, one without fallbacks and one
  with the ligature on; FALLBACK shows the fallback is not dead (VT323 lacks Ж, the engine font
  carries it) and holds every non-ASCII character in a screen's string literals and the
  content's text to being carried by one face or named in `FONT_NO_FACE`, refusing a fabricated
  one; METRICS holds the helpers to the face's own line and shows the variation's differs; SCAN
  refuses `ThemeDB.fallback_font` in any `.gd` under `godot/ui/` or `godot/presentation/` but
  `chrome.gd`, comments stripped, and is shown both ways on fabricated sources; LADDER reads every
  `*SIZE`/`*FONT`/`*SMALL`/`*TIGHT` int const and every literal size in a `draw_string` or
  `get_string_size` call — 59 today — and refuses one off the ladder, a fabricated 18 both ways.
  The sabotage pass turned it red nine ways before this landed: no fallbacks, a wrong font path,
  the ligature on, the cache removed, a ✓ in a legend row, the variation's metrics in the
  helper, the engine font named in `paperdoll.gd`, a const at 18, a call at 22. **What is not
  what the plan said, and what is half-shipped:** the engine's fallback font (Open Sans) does
  **not** carry → ▲ ▼ ↔ either — the plan and docs/30 assumed it did — so on a desktop build
  those four reach the screen through the operating system's own font fallback, exactly as they
  did before this slice, and a web build, which has none, draws a box for them now as it did
  then; they are named in `FONT_NO_FACE` with that reason, ▲ ▼ ↔ go when "The shell's rows are
  buttons" turns the bench arrows into kit glyphs, and → in the bench's offer line stays until
  something replaces it. 30 is not pixel-exact: its strokes land 1 and 2 px wide, visible under a
  magnifier, and whether the HUD and the rows should drop to a crisp 25 or climb to 50 is the
  owner's to judge (HANDOFF.md). And a 1280 × 720 window still has layout that predates the
  typeface and is not this slice's: the work panel's fixed 1520 px, the inventory sheet's
  columns, the quick strip's six slots and the corner doll over the action bar, measured the
  same against the S1 tree.

- **UI — keys wear keycaps, 2026-09-25.** The third piece of the "UI Field Kit, live" group to land
  ([docs/30](30-decisions.md#the-ui-field-kit-live-2026-09-25)). The action bar draws every key it
  names as the kit's keycap (`Chrome.keycap`, at the kit's native 1×) with its words after it: E, T
  and H from `action_line`'s own clauses, whose prose is unchanged, and each key of the standing hint,
  still the one unchanged `var keys: String` line `check_inventory` reads. What the bar draws is a
  pure list, `Hud.keycaps(action, tail)` — a clause split at " — ", a hint token split at its first
  lowercase word so "- = speed" is two keys — laid out by a pure `Hud.fit_bar`, which keeps the
  one-rung step-down "One typeface" gave the bar and then, where a cap's rim and padding still
  overrun the window (a 1280 window with the cupboard's clause did), drops the hint's tokens from
  its end, down to F1, never a clause. A cap's label sits a rung below its words, and the bar grew
  from the alpha shell's 48 px to 56 so a cap clears the frame's ten-pixel border. The centring
  measures caps with a named copy of `Chrome.keycap`'s arithmetic, but the draw advances by the width
  `keycap` returns, so drift could only move the centring. The word menu gains a gutter of the
  kit's 16 px glyphs by verb prefix — use, drop, inspect and look at, search and open, walk and
  move — present only when some row has one, and part of `ItemMenu.size_of`, so `verb_rects` and
  `draw_menu` still share one layout (`check_context`'s click lane unchanged and green).
  **Gated** by `godot:check:ui_skin`'s KEYCAPS lane, replacing its stub: every cap `keycaps` gives
  for the idle bar and for a real `action_line` with E, T and H all live is a key `input_map.gd`
  binds (BINDINGS' legend column and `INTERACT_KEY`) and one the F1 legend names, carries no digit
  unless it is a function key's name, and the tail rebuilt from the caps is the line; `fit_bar`
  lays out all nine idle caps at 1920 and a prefix keeping E and F1 inside the room at 1280;
  `_draw_action_bar`, comments stripped, reaches `fit_bar(keycaps(_action, keys))` and
  `Chrome.keycap(`; the menu is wider by exactly its gutter when a glyph verb joins and not at all
  when none does, every prefix finds a glyph that resolves, and `draw_menu` reaches `Chrome.glyph(`.
  A fabricated "3 boards", "Q quit", an unbound lead, a keyless token, a keycap only in a comment
  and a bar drawing a list of its own are each refused; `keycap` and `glyph` left HELPERS' pending
  list. The sabotage pass turned it red eleven ways, among them "3 pause" in the key line — which
  `check_inventory`'s lone-digit exemption passes and this lane refuses. **Not what the plan said,
  or left open:** at 1280 × 720 the bar keeps F1 through Esc and drops the O and M hints; the
  corner doll still overlaps the bar's left end there, as "One typeface" recorded; and "open the
  door" wears the search glyph, because the spec maps every "open" to it.

- **UI — bubbles and the dashboard in kit frames, 2026-09-25.** The fourth piece of the "UI Field

  outliers Chrome's panel/cell/item_plate/header trio never reached now frame themselves through
  `Chrome.frame`: `main.gd`'s `_draw_bubbles` plate is `Chrome.frame(self, plate, "panel_tooltip",

  and a new static `_bubble_plate` helper pads the plate up to those margins (`Chrome.Kit.margins`,
  at the owner's 2×) rather than losing the frame, the bottom edge still anchored just above the

  three housings are kit frames too — `panel_standard` for the car cluster, `panel_inset` for the
  smaller handlebar and board — each falling back to its old PANEL/RIM rect under the margins; the
  dials, needles, lamps, letters and charge bar inside them are untouched. **Gated** by
  `godot:check:ui_skin`'s OUTLIERS lane, replacing its stub: it follows `_draw_bubbles`,
  `_draw_cluster`, `_draw_handlebar` and `_draw_board` to `Chrome.frame(`, sizes a representative
  one-line bubble through `_bubble_plate` itself and checks it clears `panel_tooltip`'s margins,
  and refuses a call only in a comment, a rect-only body and a plate shrunk under the margins — all
  four sabotaged and confirmed red before being restored. HELPERS' pending list is empty with this
  piece: `frame` has real callers in both files. `godot:check:speech`, `godot:m2:vehicles` (its
  DASH lane unchanged), `godot:check:hud`, `godot:check:play` and `godot:check:appearance` stay
  green.

- **UI — empty slots say what goes there, 2026-09-25.** The fifth piece of the "UI Field Kit, live"
  group to land ([docs/30](30-decisions.md#the-ui-field-kit-live-2026-09-25)). The twelve
  equipment slots draw through kit slot styles — `slot_empty` normally, `slot_selected` when the

  numerals untouched; the bag grid's selection ring is `slot_selected`, falling back to its old
  accent ring only under the margins; and the survivor, inspect and bag headers gain a small glyph

  `Chrome.glyph` — the slice was built while `frame` still waited on its first caller and carried
  private copies of it; they were folded back into the one helper when the pieces merged, because
  three copies of the snap-style-draw arithmetic are the drift `ui/chrome.gd` exists to prevent.
  **Gated** by `godot:check:ui_skin`'s GLYPHS lane, replacing its stub: every one of the
  manifest's 32 glyphs sits in exactly one of `READERS`, `PENDING_GLYPHS` and `UNUSED_GLYPHS`; the
  twelve equipment glyphs are proved by reading `LEFT_SLOTS` and `RIGHT_SLOTS` off
  `inventory_panel.gd` and following `_draw_body` to `Chrome.glyph(`; the header readers by a
  position-aware scan that needs the name at the call's `glyph_name` argument — a first draft that
  matched any argument would have read `settings_panel.gd`'s own "settings" title as a consumed

  keycaps" reads them by, checked to carry each into a file that reaches `Chrome.glyph(`. A glyph
  in no list or two, a commented call, a call for another glyph, a label mistaken for a glyph, a
  table missing the glyph and a pending glyph with a live caller are each refused; the table path
  was sabotaged ("drop" remapped) and went red. `glyph_close` joins `glyph_lock` and `glyph_rotate`
  unused, with its reason: the sheet has no close hint yet to draw it beside (the mockup's "Tab ·
  Close" title bar is not built). `godot:check:inventory`, `:hud`, `:respond`, `:appearance` and
  `:context` stay green, with `if not _open:` → `QuickStrip.draw_strip`, `column_labels()`,
  `_draw` → `_draw_body(` → `_draw_responses(` and `Appearance.item_look` unchanged.

- **UI — the shell's rows are buttons, 2026-09-25.** The sixth piece of the "UI Field Kit, live"

  `settings_panel.gd`'s slider tracks draw the kit's `control_slider_rail.png` by hand — a control
  with no `nine_slice_ltrb`, so two end caps at its own pixels and a stretched middle — and its

  `legend.gd`, `work_panel.gd` and `web_panel.gd` gain the `journal`, `work` and `skills` header
